cover.subtitle: Faction rules, corrected cards, Leader Skills and Advanced Stronghold Cards for the second GF9 expansion. Read with the GF9 core rulebook.
cover.supportingText: Gale Force Nine rules, with source references and recorded Dune Zone judgements.

V3J3.text: Add CHOAM and Richese to the available factions. Leader Skills and Advanced Stronghold Cards are independent optional modules; choose either, both or neither, regardless of the factions selected. Stronghold Cards are Advanced game only.

cellsByColumnId.column-2: 2 sets, each with a shield, sheet, player marker, 5 standard leaders, 20 troops and 2 Alliance cards.
10 unique Treachery Cards kept outside the normal deck and hand, plus No-Field tokens numbered 0, 3 and 5.
A two-sided Inflation token and the additional Auditor leader for Advanced play.
11 cards including the Auditor. Only include the Auditor in Advanced games and remove all absent-faction cards.
2 additions.
14 optional cards.
6 optional Advanced cards, including the Ixian Hidden Mobile Stronghold.

1 corrected Poison Tooth and 1 corrected Artillery Strike replace their Ixians & Tleilaxu copies; if that expansion is absent, add these 2 cards. Replace the 2 core Karama cards with the updated cards.

4DJU.text: The Treachery discard pile is private. Do not search or inspect it unless a card or ability explicitly permits it. Discarded Richese cards enter the ordinary discard pile and may later be reshuffled into the main Treachery Deck.

HLFJ.text: Start with 5 spice and all 20 troops in reserves. Free revival is 2 troops. Keep the 10 Richese Treachery Cards in a separate cache; they do not count as cards in your hand. Keep No-Field tokens 0, 3 and 5.

SPAB.text: Each Bidding round, replace one normal auction card with a revealed card chosen from your cache. Before Ixians use Bidding, announce whether your cache card will be the first or last auction of the round. Sell it by Once Around or Silent Auction, ignoring normal bidding order.

VHJF.text: Other factions pay you for cache cards. If you buy your own card, pay the Emperor, or the Spice Bank if the Emperor is absent. Karama cannot buy or acquire a cache-auction card. If everyone else declines to pay, you may take the card free or remove it from the game.

G89X.text: The cache is used only when Richese is playing. Do not shuffle all cache cards into the starting Treachery Deck as a substitute for Richese auctions.

cellsByColumnId.column-2: Choose clockwise or counter-clockwise. Begin with the adjacent faction on that side. Each eligible faction may pass or place a higher bid exactly once. When the opportunity reaches Richese, Richese either outbids the current high bid and buys, or the high bidder buys. Juice of Sappho can change who bids last.

Every eligible faction secretly holds any amount of spice, including zero, in one hand. Reveal simultaneously. The largest amount wins; break ties in storm order. If all amounts are zero, Richese may take the card free or remove it.

SZRB.text: Harkonnen receive their usual free extra card after buying either a cache card or Black Market card. The Ixian alliance replacement applies to Black Market purchases, but not to the separate cache auction.

7T56.text: Reduce the normal auction supply for each Richese card replacing a normal card. If Ixians are playing, they still draw one more than the reduced number of normal cards, inspect the draw, return one to the deck and shuffle the rest. If the cache card is first, auction it before the Ixian Bidding advantage; if last, reveal and auction it after normal bidding.

68ZB.text: Richese may contribute to an ally's bid, including a Silent bid. That contribution goes to the Emperor, or the Bank if absent; the ally's own share goes to Richese. Richese must already hold its contribution and cannot count the incoming payment to fund it. A full hand cannot enter the auction. A Black Market card purchased before Declaration counts in that player's declared hand.

ALYN.text: Sources: choam-richese, p. 5; choam-richese, p. 10; choam-richese, p. 11.

YKRD.text: Instead of a normal shipment, pay the cost of shipping one troop and place an available No-Field token face down in the destination. Use the normal rate of 1 spice to a stronghold or 2 elsewhere, paid to the Guild or the Spice Bank. Until revealed the token counts as one troop for all effects, even when its hidden number is 0.

7UT8.text: Move the token as a troop. Before the Battle phase, you may reveal it voluntarily. Replace it with its number of troops from reserves, or all remaining reserves if fewer are available. A storm or worm reveals it and destroys that number of troops, limited by available reserves.

XDRH.text: In a battle involving the token, reveal it with your Battle Plan and bring in that many available reserve troops. You cannot dial more than the troops available to reveal. Atreides cannot ask to see your number dialed in this battle. A 0 token still permits normal leader and Treachery Card choices.

8WBW.text: Only one No-Field token may be on Arrakis at once. Do not use the same numbered token twice consecutively for yourself or an ally. Keep the last used token face up in front of your shield until another is placed.

WGDB.text: An unrevealed token collects spice as one troop. Entering a stronghold with a Terror token can trigger that token, including with No-Field 0. Revealing an already-present No-Field does not trigger Terror again. If Trip to Gamont targets a No-Field, reveal it and return one revealed troop to reserves, if present; Trip to Gamont is used even if none is revealed.

VCAH.text: Sources: choam-richese, p. 6; choam-richese, p. 10; choam-richese, p. 11.

XWKZ.text: You may offer to ship an ally's reserve troops using an available No-Field token. Reveal any token already on Arrakis first. Pay for shipping one troop, then immediately reveal the new token and place up to its number of the ally's available reserve troops. Either ally may pay the shipment cost. Keep the used token face up to prevent consecutive reuse. This triggers Heighliners unless the shipped faction is the Guild.

BTJY.text: You may give your ally a Richese Treachery Card from your hand at any time while the ally has room. This transfers a card already in your hand, not one directly out of the cache.

MPG3.text: Advanced Black Market: before Bidding Declaration, you may offer one card from your hand. You may describe it truthfully or lie, but do not show it; Atreides may still inspect it. Choose normal bidding, Once Around or Silent Auction. Karama cannot acquire it. If nobody bids spice, keep the card and end the intervention. If it sells, receive the payment and remove one normal card from that round's auction supply. After normal-method bidding, resume where normal bidding left off; after an alternative auction, resume in storm order.

BLDH.text: Richese occupation of Tuek's Sietch also prevents the Fremen special victory, alongside Atreides, Harkonnen and Emperor occupation. This applies in both Basic and Advanced play.

7BQR.text: Advanced special Karama: once per game, spend a Karama Card and 3 spice to secretly choose and buy one card remaining in your Richese cache at any time.

Q534.text: Start with 2 spice and all 20 troops in reserves. You have no free revival, but you may pay to revive any number of your troops for 1 spice each.

QE7H.text: At the start of CHOAM Charity, before anyone else collects, take 2 spice from the Spice Bank for each faction in the game. Pay other factions' normal Charity from your own spice. This income alone does not trigger the Spice Production Tech Token.

NMTQ.text: During a Mentat Pause you may place Inflation on the Charity phase, either Double or Cancel side up. In the next turn, double or cancel Charity for that turn, including your own faction income and Advanced Bene Gesserit Charity. In the next Mentat Pause flip it. After the second affected turn, remove it from the game instead of flipping again.

JQZ2.text: No spice bribes can be made while Double is face up in play. Tech Token income stays unchanged and is paid by the Spice Bank. Homeworld extra Charity is paid by the Spice Bank when its faction actually qualifies for Charity.

QP3L.text: Sources: choam-richese, p. 7; choam-richese, p. 8; choam-richese, p. 10.

ALCY.text: Your hand limit is 5 Treachery Cards. At the end of any phase, reveal exact duplicate cards in your hand and discard surplus copies for 3 spice each. A Snooper, Portable Snooper and Shield Snooper are three different cards. You may also discard any Worthless Card for 2 spice without needing a duplicate.

4DNK.text: Instead of spice, discard a Worthless Card for its named effect at the moment that effect applies. An effect reacting to movement, revival, storm or Karama is used when that event is attempted.

cellsByColumnId.column-2: Prevent one player from moving troops into a territory you occupy during Shipment and Movement. Shipment is still allowed.
Prevent your troop losses in one territory from one storm movement.
When one player attempts a Karama, prevent that player from playing Karama for the rest of the phase. The prevented card stays in their hand.
Move your troops one additional territory during your movement.
Prevent one player from taking free revival during Revival.
During Mentat Pause, return one troop belonging to another player to that player's reserves, before checking victory.

SJAQ.text: Advanced special Karama: once per game, spend a Karama Card at any time to discard any number of other Treachery Cards from your hand for 3 spice each, including Worthless Cards. This is one use, not an ongoing power.

LV6F.text: Sources: choam-richese, p. 4; choam-richese, p. 7; choam-richese, p. 10.

S97N.text: Once per turn, at the end of any phase, you and your ally may exchange one Treachery Card each. It must be a two-way exchange. You may also pay some or all of your ally's spice support in battle; that payment goes to the Spice Bank.

WSP4.text: Advanced Auditor: add the strength-2 Auditor to your leaders and its Traitor Card to the deck. After a battle in which you used it, audit your opponent's unused hand cards at random: 2 if the Auditor survived or 1 if it died. The opponent may pay you 1 spice for each card you could actually inspect to cancel the whole audit. Partial payment cannot reduce the audit.

ZPFM.text: The Auditor cannot be captured, taken as a Tleilaxu ghola or assigned a Leader Skill. You may revive it as your one leader revival for the turn regardless of your other leaders' availability. It always returns face up to the Tanks when killed.

QV4M.text: Advanced troop support income: when another faction pays spice to support troops in a battle, receive half its total payment rounded down; the remainder goes to the Spice Bank. Count spice supplied by the Arrakeen Stronghold Card. Your own support payments go to the Bank. If any traitor is revealed in that battle, receive no support income.

U5T4.title: Optional Leader Skill setup | Optional module

2BN3.text: Use the 14-card Leader Skill Deck. After faction positions and the Bene Gesserit prediction, deal starting Treachery Cards, including the Ixian starting selection and Harkonnen extra card. Deal 2 Leader Skill Cards to each faction. Keep one and shuffle the other back into the Skill Deck.

H8ZA.text: Place the chosen skill face up in front of your shield and assign one of your eligible leader discs beside it. Then complete Traitor selection and the remaining setup. CHOAM's Auditor cannot receive a skill.

DSZA.text: A skill remains assigned for that leader's life. Its general effect works while both card and leader are face up in front of your shield. Use a Leader Skill before the corresponding faction ability, for example Mentat before Atreides Prescience.

G54W.title: Leader Skills in battle and revival | Optional module

UNKE.text: When selecting a battle leader, leave the skilled leader and card face up, or take both behind your shield. Leaving them face up keeps the general effect available where applicable. If you take them behind the shield but use a different leader, neither part of that skill applies in that battle.

2WME.text: When fighting with the skilled leader, include the Leader Skill Card in your Battle Plan. Its general effect and battle effect apply as written, unless the leader is killed in the battle. Return a surviving leader and its skill in front of the shield after battle. A Mentat may use its pre-plan effect and then enter the battle.

S5HF.text: A skill naming a card type requires the card actually to be played as that type. Chemistry must be used as a poison weapon for a poison-weapon bonus. Zoal copies only the opposing leader's printed value, never skill bonuses.

CVPB.text: If the skilled leader dies, shuffle its skill into the Skill Deck. When you later revive one of your own leaders while you have no skill, you may draw 2, choose one for that revived leader, and return the other to the deck. Tleilaxu acquiring another faction's ghola do not get this draw.

GA2K.text: A captured leader takes the skill with it, but Harkonnen may use only that leader's battle skill while it fights, not passive general effects. Rihani Decipherer gives Tleilaxu a Face Dancer and can replace only an unrevealed Face Dancer. Smuggler can add its free troop to a No-Field shipment into an empty territory. Spice Banker can trigger on a qualifying revival payment to the Spice Bank.

EQVU.text: Sources: choam-richese, p. 9; choam-richese, p. 11; choam-richese, p. 12.

F6V8.title: Optional Advanced Stronghold Cards | Advanced game

SNDH.text: Use the 6-card Stronghold Deck only in the Advanced game. No one begins with a Stronghold Card, even when starting troops occupy its location. During the first Mentat Pause and each later Mentat Pause, give each card to the sole occupant of its stronghold, ignoring Bene Gesserit advisors. If nobody controls the stronghold, set its card aside.

N378.text: Keep the card until the next Mentat Pause; moving away, losing the stronghold or flipping to advisors does not transfer it immediately. A card can therefore remain with a faction that no longer occupies its location until that check.

cellsByColumnId.column-2: The Spice Bank pays 2 spice toward your troop support in a battle here.
If you play no poison weapon in a battle here, any non-poison defense you play also functions as a Snooper.
Win tied battles here, overriding storm order and Juice of Sappho.
Before Battle Plans, choose another Stronghold Card you control and copy its ability for this battle.
After winning here, take spice from the Bank equal to the opponent's dial, rounded down.
Gain 2 spice from the Bank per Worthless Card you play in a battle here.
Distrans - Give another player a treachery card from your hand at any time except during a bid and if their hand size permits. Discard after use.

Choose one: (1) be considered aggressor in a battle or (2) play at the beginning of a phase or action that requires turn order to go first or (3) go last in a phase or action that requires turn order. Discard after use. The battle-aggressor option may be played after Battle Plans are revealed; other choices apply at their stated turn-order window.
Weapon - Special - Play as part of your Battle Plan. Becomes a copy of your opponent's weapon. Discard after use.
Defense - Poison - You may play this after revealing your battle plan if you did not play a defense and if Voice permits. Discard after use.
Ornithopter - As part of your movement you may move one group of forces up to 3 territories or two groups of forces up to your normal move distance. Discard after use.
Nullentropy Box - At any time, pay 2 spice to secretly search and take one card from the treachery discard pile. Then shuffle the discard pile, discarding this card on top.
Semuta Drug - Add a treachery card to your hand immediately after another player discards it. You choose if multiple cards are discarded at the same time. Discard after use.
Residual Poison - Play against your opponent in battle before making battle plans. Kills one of their available leaders at random. No spice is collected for it. Discard after use.

Weapon - Special - Play as part of your Battle Plan. You choose after plans are revealed to either kill both leaders or reduce the strength of both leaders to 0. The player with the highest number of undialed forces wins the battle. Dialed forces are lost normally. Discard after use.
Uses the updated Karama rules. It begins in the 10-card Richese cache rather than the main deck.

RG2R.text: Nullentropy Box cannot retrieve itself. Its selection stays secret. A Richese card discarded after purchase joins ordinary Treachery discards rather than returning to the cache. The cache card named Karama is in addition to the two updated cards replacing the core copies.

F8WB.text: Sources: choam-richese, p. 5; choam-richese, p. 10; choam-richese, p. 11.

T6GF.text: Poison Tooth replaces the earlier version. It kills both leaders and is not stopped by a Snooper. After seeing battle results, you may choose not to activate it. A winner may retain it only if it was not used. Otherwise discard it. Chemistry played as a poison defense can protect against it.

WWLP.text: Artillery Strike replaces the earlier version. It kills both leaders unless their Shields protect them. A surviving shielded leader contributes no leader strength; the higher dial wins. Collect no spice for any leader killed in that battle, however it died. Discard Artillery Strike after use.

HUTU.text: The updated Karama replaces one use of a faction advantage, including an alliance ability, after setup. For battle advantages it must be played before Battle Plans are revealed. Other uses are a Guild-rate shipment paid to the Bank, an eligible normal Treachery auction acquisition, or your once-per-game special power. It cannot acquire Richese auctions, cancel a special victory or cancel a special Karama power.

cellsByColumnId.column-2: Stop the special collection; ordinary qualifying Charity remains, paid by the Bank.
Prevent a discard for spice, or the relevant Worthless effect.
Limit the relevant revival to the normal rate and limit, with an allowed Tleilaxu increase if applicable.
Prevent placing the token. Do not stop a required later flip.
Prevent support income for one battle.
Prevent one audit.
Prevent the cache auction at the start of the round.
Prevent the No-Field shipment.
Prevent the sale from hand.

In the unofficial revised book, the printed rule-page number is two less than the PDF page number. Named references, such as a faction sheet or skin.json entry, identify a section or file location.

item-2.text: gf9-faq-2020-11 and faq-nov2020 mean Dune Questions and Answers, Gale Force Nine, November 2020, 9 PDF pages. Its clarifications inform the rules; its questions and answers are not reproduced here.

item-3.text: gf9-ixian-tleilaxu and ixian-tleilaxu mean Dune: Ixians & Tleilaxu Rulebook, Gale Force Nine, 2020 expansion, 12 PDF pages.

item-4.text: gf9-choam-richese and choam-richese mean Dune: CHOAM & Richese Rulebook, Gale Force Nine, supplied 2021 expansion copy, 12 PDF pages.

item-5.text: gf9-ecaz-moritani and ecaz-moritani mean Dune: Ecaz & Moritani Rulebook, Gale Force Nine, supplied copy with 2022 copyright, 16 PDF pages.

item-6.text: revised-v2.3 means Unofficial Revised Dune Rulebook by Van Willis, the supplied file named v2.3. Its internal heading says Version 2.2. It has 44 PDF pages and marks unofficial changes with outlined text. It is a comparison reference, not a new official edition.

item-7.text: compilation means Dune Boardgame Rules Compilation, assembled by Johannes Cassebaum for the Dune Tabletop Discord server, supplied undated copy, 46 PDF pages. It combines the base game, first two expansions and published questions and answers.

item-8.text: treachery-online means the treachery.online community implementation and card reference files by Ronald Ossendrijver and contributors. File locations identify the referenced data, rather than a printed page.

EMQ3.text: The source copies and community references are linked from the GF9 source ticket: https://github.com/ndelangen/dunezone/issues/2216. The supplied copies identify what was read; a mirror or filename alone does not establish the latest official printing.

RCQR.text: Conflicting statements and the interpretation adopted for Dune Zone are recorded in GF9 judgements: https://github.com/ndelangen/dunezone/issues/2352. Specific expansion rules apply within their scope. Explicit corrections replace the text they correct. Where the sources disagree, consult that record for the decision, reasons and affected content.

cover.subtitle: Learn and play Gale Force Nine's Dune with the six original factions. This reference follows the Basic Game, identifies Advanced Game additions, and places faction exceptions beside the rules they affect. Expansion factions and optional modules have separate companion books.
cover.supportingText: Gale Force Nine rules, with source references and recorded Dune Zone judgements.

GFGQ.text: Each player leads a faction competing for control of Arrakis. Spice pays for cards, shipment and revival. Leaders, weapons and traitors decide battles, while the storm controls movement and turn order. You can win alone or form a public alliance with one other faction.

G7MH.text: Play up to ten turns. At the Mentat Pause, an unallied faction normally wins by occupying at least three strongholds. A two-faction alliance normally needs four distinct strongholds between its members. Check victory after battles and spice collection, not as soon as a force enters a stronghold.

N6GF.text: The five original strongholds are Arrakeen, Carthag, Sietch Tabr, Habbanya Sietch and Tuek's Sietch. A faction occupies a stronghold with at least one force that counts for occupation. Advanced Bene Gesserit advisors do not count.

5DFL.title: Learn the Basic Game first
5DFL.text: The Basic Game uses the common rules and basic faction advantages. The Advanced Game adds double spice blows, spice support in battle, stronghold income, advanced faction advantages and special Karama powers. Expansion factions and optional modules have their own books.

4U5C.text: A specific faction advantage or card effect changes the general rule only where it says so. Apply the rest of the general rule normally.

695W.text: An advantage saying may or can gives a choice. Carry out mandatory effects as written, such as the Harkonnen bonus card after a purchase when there is room.

QKVG.text: Sources: gf9-base-2019, p. 6; gf9-base-2019, p. 11; gf9-base-2019, p. 13; gf9-base-2019, p. 18.

VDK2.text: Territories are named areas with borders. Sand territories have single borders, rock double borders, and strongholds triple borders. The Polar Sink is the central safe area. Eighteen radial sectors divide the board for storm movement, spice placement and spice collection.

8ZAD.text: A territory can span several sectors. Keep each group in a particular sector. Forces in different sectors of the same territory can normally move or fight together, unless the storm separates them. Moving to another sector of the same territory uses your normal force movement.

BMC7.text: The storm moves counterclockwise around the outer edge. Sand forces and spice in sectors it crosses are vulnerable. Rock, strongholds and the Polar Sink protect forces from storm losses, but a sector currently under the storm still blocks shipment, movement and battle. Imperial Basin is the protected sand exception.

8DBZ.text: Keep dead forces and leaders in the Tleilaxu Tanks. Keep living reserves off the board beside your shield. The Spice Bank supplies spice and receives payments unless a faction or card redirects them. The turn track records the current turn.

CPYT.text: Sources: gf9-base-2019, p. 4; gf9-base-2019, p. 7; gf9-base-2019, p. 10; gf9-faq-2020-11, p. 2.

APH4.text: Each base faction has a shield, reference sheet, player marker, twenty force tokens and five leader discs. A leader's printed number is its battle strength and normal revival cost. The character on a faction shield represents the faction and is not an additional leader disc.

cellsByColumnId.column-3: Territory spice blows and Shai-Hulud sandworms

5JEJ.text: Set out spice tokens, both battle wheels, the storm marker, turn counter and Destroyed Shield Wall token. The Advanced Game also uses the Kwisatz Haderach card and counter, the Fremen sandworm token, three Fedaykin and five Sardaukar. Starred tokens count as ordinary forces in the Basic Game.

8ASE.text: Agree whether to play Basic or Advanced, which expansion factions are available, and which optional modules are in use. Owning an expansion does not require using all its modules. Keep cards for unused modules out of their decks.

63UT.text: The expanded faction selection still assumes a game of at most six players. Larger groups can experiment, but adding factions does not by itself add player circles, strongholds or a revised winning target.

G5ED.text: For three players, GF9 recommends Atreides, Harkonnen and Fremen. A three-player alliance still needs four strongholds. For four players, consider leaving out Spacing Guild and Bene Gesserit; for five, consider leaving out Bene Gesserit.

FAY4.text: For two players, try Atreides against Harkonnen, or have each player control two factions. GF9 increases the winning requirement to four strongholds for a two-player game. Keep the factions' hands, spice, forces and rules separate when controlling more than one.

MGFT.text: The default alliance limit is two factions and its winning requirement is four strongholds. Other alliance arrangements are optional and must be agreed before play.

EZ4P.text: Sources: gf9-base-2019, p. 6; gf9-base-2019, p. 24; gf9-ecaz-moritani, p. 9.

item-1.text: Put all spice in the Spice Bank. Shuffle the Spice and Treachery decks separately and place them face down beside the board. Leave room for discards.

item-2.text: Choose factions. You can deal random faction prediction cards, or draw numbered prediction cards and choose factions from highest number to lowest. Players may agree to swap.

item-3.text: Place each player marker in the circle nearest that player's shield and seat. The circles determine storm order. Bene Gesserit now secretly records its faction and turn prediction.

item-4.text: Remove traitor cards for factions not playing. Shuffle and deal four to each player. Each normally chooses one and returns the other three face down to the bottom of the Traitor Deck. Harkonnen keeps all four. A player may keep a card for their own leader to protect that leader from selection by another player.

item-5.text: Give each faction its starting spice and place its starting forces as described below. Put its remaining forces in reserves.

item-6.text: Deal one Treachery Card to each faction, except Harkonnen receives two. Keep hands secret. Expansion setup can alter this dealing procedure.

item-7.text: Place the turn counter at 1. Resolve the first storm using the special first-turn procedure.

ZMEW.text: If using Leader Skills, that module moves the starting Treachery deal before traitor selection. Ixians, Tleilaxu, Ecaz and Moritani also have setup instructions; follow the appropriate expansion book when they are in play.

UFV7.text: Sources: gf9-base-2019, p. 6; gf9-base-2019, p. 17; gf9-base-2019, p. 18; gf9-choam-richese, p. 8; gf9-ixian-tleilaxu, p. 6; gf9-ixian-tleilaxu, p. 8.

cellsByColumnId.column-2: 10 in Arrakeen
1 in Polar Sink
None on Arrakis
10 divided between Sietch Tabr, False Wall South and False Wall West
cellsByColumnId.column-3: 10 on the far side of Dune

cellsByColumnId.column-2: 10 in Carthag
5 in Tuek's Sietch

VLEH.text: In the Advanced Game, Bene Gesserit places only one starting advisor in any territory after the Fremen placement. If alone, it immediately becomes a fighter. This replaces the Basic starting force in Polar Sink; it does not add a second force.

CFU6.text: Advanced Emperor has fifteen ordinary forces and five Sardaukar; Advanced Fremen has seventeen ordinary forces and three Fedaykin. These are parts of the twenty-force supply.

VPHH.text: Keep spice behind your shield. Keep your hand and selected traitors secret if you wish. You may voluntarily tell or show information to another player, publicly or privately, unless a particular effect forbids it. Information sharing does not transfer ownership of a card.

HFZK.text: During Bidding, everyone must disclose the number of Treachery Cards in their hand. Their identities remain private. The normal hand limit is four; Harkonnen's is eight. You cannot bid with a full hand, including when holding Karama.

QYEL.text: Atreides alone may make written records about Treachery Cards. Other notes about the game may be kept privately under GF9's general clarification. Tournament restrictions on notes are separate rules.

R698.text: Discarded cards are placed face up, but the discard pile may not be searched unless an effect allows it. Watching a discard happen does not give permission to look through the pile later. When a deck is exhausted, reshuffle its discards; in the Advanced Game combine both Spice discard piles for the reshuffle.

KHYQ.text: Sources: gf9-base-2019, p. 6; gf9-base-2019, p. 8; gf9-base-2019, p. 12; gf9-faq-2020-11, p. 2; gf9-faq-2020-11, p. 7; gf9-faq-2020-11, p. 9; gf9-choam-richese, p. 4.

CSCB.title: The nine phases of a turn

cellsByColumnId.column-2: Move the storm, remove losses and determine First Player.
Reveal spice cards; resolve worms and any alliance opportunity.
Eligible factions take charity.
Auction Treachery Cards.
Return eligible dead forces and leaders to play.
Each player ships once, then moves one group.
Resolve all required battles.
Collect spice with surviving forces.
Collect deferred bribes and check victory; advance the turn if needed.

QAZV.text: First Player is the faction whose player marker the storm will next approach while continuing counterclockwise. Proceed to that player's right, counterclockwise, when an activity calls for storm order. In battle, the earliest involved faction in that order is the aggressor.

MGQE.title: The nine phases of a turn, continued

222V.text: Complete one phase before beginning the next. A card or faction ability can introduce a specific action within a phase; it does not give permission to skip the remaining sequence.

9UQB.text: Sources: gf9-base-2019, p. 7; gf9-base-2019, p. 10; gf9-base-2019, p. 12; gf9-faq-2020-11, p. 3.

C7JT.text: Place the storm at the Storm Start sector. The players whose circles are nearest on either side of that sector each secretly dial a number from zero through twenty. Reveal both numbers together, add them, and move the storm counterclockwise that many sectors.

7DEF.text: This procedure determines the first storm position and turn order. Resolve storm losses in sectors crossed under the normal storm rule. In an Advanced Game with Fremen, use this same first storm procedure; the Fremen Storm Deck takes over on later turns.

8DJH.text: On turns two onward, the two players who last used the battle wheels secretly dial one, two or three. Reveal together, add the numbers and move the storm counterclockwise that many sectors.

XNQA.text: If Advanced Fremen is playing, reveal the Storm Card it selected during the preceding turn instead. Move that many sectors, return the card, shuffle the Storm Deck, and let Fremen secretly select and inspect the card for the next turn. Without Advanced Fremen, continue using the two dials.

QRSR.text: Weather Control can replace the calculated movement. After turn one, its player chooses zero through ten sectors and discards the card. The card can be played after the ordinary distance is known, but before the storm moves. Family Atomics also has a window before movement.

Z47U.text: Sources: gf9-base-2019, p. 7; gf9-base-2019, p. 16; gf9-faq-2020-11, p. 1.

3DCK.text: Send forces in crossed or final sectors of sand territories to the Tanks. Imperial Basin is protected while the Shield Wall stands. Forces in rock, strongholds and the Polar Sink survive normal storm movement. Return spice in sectors crossed or stopped on to the Bank.

66PB.text: Forces cannot ship, move or battle into, out of or through the sector currently under the storm. In a territory spanning several sectors, a group may enter or leave an uncovered part if its path does not cross the covered part. The Polar Sink is never covered.

T822.text: Forces in different parts of one territory cannot battle if separated by the storm. Two factions can therefore survive in the same stronghold while it is blocked; neither counts that disputed stronghold toward victory.

GCVA.title: Advanced Fremen exception
GCVA.text: In the Advanced Game, Fremen loses half the forces caught in the storm, rounding losses up. It can bring reserves into its permitted landing area under storm at the same half loss. This exception permits reserve placement, not ordinary movement or a worm ride into or out of the storm.

9UEM.text: Turn over the top Spice Card. For a territory card, take the printed amount of spice from the Bank and place it in that territory's sector marked with the spice-blow symbol. If that sector is under the storm, place no spice. Put the card face up on the Spice discard pile.

AY25.text: On the first turn, set every revealed Shai-Hulud card aside and keep drawing until the required territory card appears. Those set-aside worms have no effect and cause no Nexus. Shuffle them back into the Spice Deck after the phase.

LCSM.text: In the Basic Game, resolve one spice blow each turn. In the Advanced Game, resolve two, keeping separate discard piles A and B. Apply a worm to the territory on top of its own pile, not the other pile.

T58U.text: After turn one, a Shai-Hulud card devours the spice and forces in the territory shown on the card previously on top of that discard pile. Return spice to the Bank and forces to the Tanks. The attack is against that previous blow, not the new spice about to appear.

EA7V.text: Discard the worm on that pile and draw again. Discard consecutive worms and continue until a territory card appears. Resolve that spice blow. In the Basic Game, a worm appearing during the phase provides a Nexus after the spice draw is complete. In the Advanced Game, finish that pile's draw, Nexus and riding before resolving the other pile.

6XMV.text: Fremen forces are not devoured. After the Nexus, Fremen may ride the worm with some or all of its forces at the attacked location to one destination, subject to storm and occupancy rules. A ride may end in any territory, including a stronghold; the destination need not be sand. It uses no normal movement and costs no shipment spice.

UU8F.text: Fremen can choose whether to protect its ally from being devoured. Protection does not give that ally a worm ride. Advanced Fremen can place consecutive additional worms in sand territories of its choice; resolve each such worm's destruction and the Fremen riding benefit.

item-1.text: Reveal and resolve a card using pile A. If worms appear, resolve their destruction and continue drawing until a territory card is resolved. Then hold the Nexus and resolve the Fremen rides for that pile.

item-2.text: Reveal and resolve a card using pile B with the same procedure. Its worms affect the previous territory on pile B. If that pile produces a Nexus, hold it and resolve its rides too.

item-3.text: A turn can therefore have a Nexus from each pile. Keep the piles separate until a deck reshuffle. A special Fremen Karama worm retains its own stated phase-end Nexus timing.

VNJN.text: The first-turn worm exemption applies to both draws. Atreides' next-spice inspection still reveals only the single top card, not two cards. Expansion Sandtrout, Thumper and discovery cards add instructions described in their expansion books.

DCVT.text: During a Nexus, players may discuss alliances, publicly break an existing alliance and form a new one. No faction can belong to more than one alliance. The default maximum is two factions. Declare all alliances openly and exchange alliance reminder cards.

WXBG.text: A player may leave an alliance during a Nexus without the former ally's permission. Outside a Nexus, alliances persist unless a specific expansion effect changes them. A Nexus does not compel anyone to ally.

HY6D.text: An alliance normally wins by occupying four distinct strongholds between its members at the Mentat Pause. Allies may not battle one another. Except in Polar Sink, they must not finish the applicable evacuation window sharing a territory.

FF65.text: If newly allied factions already share a territory, one must leave during Shipment and Movement. If the first to ship and move does not leave, the later ally must leave or send its forces there to the Tanks. Advanced Bene Gesserit advisors are included in this official alliance restriction. Ecaz's Occupy advantage is a specific expansion exception.

Z9DB.text: An ally may pass through a territory containing allied forces or ship there and then move out, as long as the move ends elsewhere. The rule blocking entry into a stronghold with two other factions still applies.

J2X6.text: Sources: gf9-base-2019, p. 12; gf9-base-2019, p. 23; gf9-faq-2020-11, p. 2; gf9-faq-2020-11, p. 4; gf9-ecaz-moritani, p. 8.

QG65.text: You may pay part or all of an ally's Treachery purchase or shipment, up to the actual cost. Promise that help before the ally bids beyond its own holdings. Pay the recipient of that transaction directly, rather than transferring unrestricted spice to the ally.

ZNG3.text: For a normal Treachery purchase, pay the Emperor, or the Bank if no Emperor is playing. When the Emperor itself helps its ally buy a card, the Emperor's contribution goes to the ally and is paid back to the Emperor under the official clarification.

CK27.text: For shipment, pay the Guild, or the Bank if no Guild is playing. Any contribution the Guild itself makes toward its ally's shipment goes to the Bank.

V3RR.text: Alliance does not normally let players transfer spice for other purposes, pay one another's battle support or revival, transfer cards, share leaders, or use every faction power. Each faction's alliance advantage states the further help it permits. The Emperor can give spice directly to its ally, immediately and for any purpose.

DFJ4.text: You cannot put a weapon or defense from your own hand into an ally's battle plan. Cards with independent timing, such as Truthtrance or Karama, may be played by a nonparticipant when their own instructions allow it.

JRED.text: A faction with zero or one spice may call CHOAM Charity and take enough spice to bring its total to two. This is a top-up, not two extra spice for a faction already holding one.

5PNK.text: Advanced Bene Gesserit receives two spice regardless of its existing holdings, including on turn one. If CHOAM is in play, its charity and Inflation rules change who supplies charity and its amount; use that expansion book.

2ECS.text: Spice promised by a bribe and sitting in front of a shield is not yet spendable. Do not treat it as money behind that shield before the Mentat Pause.

T8PX.text: Sources: gf9-base-2019, p. 8; gf9-base-2019, p. 18; gf9-faq-2020-11, p. 9; gf9-choam-richese, p. 7; gf9-choam-richese, p. 8.

item-1.text: Everyone declares their current hand size. Count factions with room for at least one card and deal that many cards face down in a row. Harkonnen's larger hand limit applies.

item-2.text: Atreides may inspect the card about to be auctioned before anyone bids. The First Player opens, or the next eligible player to the right if First Player's hand is full.

item-3.text: The opening bid is at least one spice, or a pass. Proceed to the right. A bid must exceed the current bid. A previous pass does not stop a player re-entering if bidding returns to them.

item-4.text: When one bidder remains and all others pass, that bidder pays and takes the card. Other factions pay the Emperor if present; the Emperor pays the Bank for its own purchase. Harkonnen also draws its bonus card if room remains.

item-5.text: The next auction opens with the first eligible faction to the right of the previous opening bidder. Repeat until the offered cards are sold or everyone passes on a card.

item-6.text: If nobody bids, return the unsold cards to the top of the Treachery Deck and end the normal auction round.

DKZC.text: You may not bid more spice than you can pay using your holdings and your ally's promised contribution, except while holding Karama. A full hand must pass even with Karama. Each bid must be made within ten seconds or it counts as a pass.

ZW4B.text: A player can acquire several cards while space remains. The number offered was determined when dealing; it is not one guaranteed purchase per player. Expansion Ixian and Richese auction procedures can alter the normal offer.

Q9EX.text: During Revival, each faction may return dead forces from the Tanks to its reserves. Its free revival allowance is shown on its sheet. Additional ordinary forces cost two spice each. Free and paid revivals together normally cannot exceed three forces per turn.

JJ9R.text: Only forces actually in the Tanks can be revived. Reserves and forces on Arrakis are already alive. Revival returns forces to reserves; getting them onto Arrakis normally requires shipment later in the turn.

3CXX.text: Fremen gets three free revivals and cannot buy additional revivals under the base rules. The Emperor may pay for up to three additional revivals for its ally. A Ghola card adds the revival stated on that card. Tleilaxu and expansion modules can change limits or costs.

ZESG.text: In the Advanced Game, no more than one Fedaykin and one Sardaukar of the respective factions may be revived per turn. Each counts as one force toward the applicable force allowance. Ghola, the Emperor's alliance and Tleilaxu do not bypass the one-special-force limit.

BCZZ.text: Leader revival is separate from force revival. If eligible, you may revive one leader as well as taking your force revivals in the same phase.

HUG7.text: Once all five of your leaders are in the Tanks, you may revive one per Revival Phase until all have been revived. Pay that leader's printed strength in spice to the Bank. The leader returns to your available leaders and remains subject to its original traitor card.

54B2.text: In Advanced play, having no leader of your own available because the others are captured also opens normal leader revival. A leader merely committed to another territory earlier in the Battle Phase does not create a Revival Phase action.

4FS7.text: When a revived leader dies again, place it face down in the Tanks. It cannot be revived again until all the faction's other revivable leaders have also been revived, killed and returned to the Tanks. Ghola and Tleilaxu may explicitly bypass normal availability restrictions.

XMTL.text: A leader revived by Ghola during Battle can fight immediately, including in that same phase. The Kwisatz Haderach is a separate Atreides token; whether it is alive or dead does not delay normal revival of the five Atreides leaders.

JNS3.text: Sources: gf9-base-2019, p. 9; gf9-base-2019, p. 17; gf9-base-2019, p. 22; gf9-faq-2020-11, p. 6.

L8PJ.text: Beginning with First Player and proceeding to the right, each faction completes its shipment and then its movement. A faction may make one shipment of any number of its reserves to one sector of one territory.

cellsByColumnId.column-2: 1 spice
2 spice

RZYV.text: Pay the Guild if it is playing, otherwise the Bank. The Guild pays its own costs to the Bank. Clearly identify the destination sector in a territory spanning several sectors. Shipment does not consume normal movement, so newly shipped forces may move immediately.

CRZZ.text: You cannot ship into the storm or into a stronghold containing two other factions. Ordinary shipment is from reserves to the board; it cannot retrieve forces or move them between board territories. Fremen's free placement and Guild cross-shipment are exceptions.

YEDF.text: You may decline shipment or movement. You still finish your own shipment opportunity before your own movement. The Advanced Guild may choose the gap between players in which it takes the complete shipment-and-movement turn.

RKL4.text: Sources: gf9-base-2019, p. 9; gf9-base-2019, p. 16; gf9-base-2019, p. 19.

QV4Q.text: For your normal movement, choose any number of your forces in one territory and move them together to one destination territory. Ordinary range is one adjacent territory. You may leave forces behind, but cannot split one movement into several destinations or gather forces from several origins.

GPYX.text: If you occupy Arrakeen or Carthag when that movement begins, you have ornithopters and may move up to three adjacent territories. The moving group can start anywhere on Arrakis. Forces just shipped into one of those cities can provide the ornithopters immediately.

DK7Q.text: Fremen normally moves two territories instead of one. It can use three-territory ornithopter movement if it has access. Ranges replace rather than add to one another.

3EGU.text: A city under the storm can still provide ornithopters for a group elsewhere. The storm does not itself switch off city access, but the moving group cannot enter, leave or cross a stormed sector.

EXF4.text: Count territory borders, not sector lines. Sectors still matter for avoiding the storm and choosing a final position. Changing sector within a territory uses movement. Forces in separate uncovered sectors of the same territory can form the moving group.

N8A9.text: Never enter or pass through a stronghold already containing two other factions. Passing through an allied territory is permitted if you finish elsewhere. Do not move into, out of or across the storm. The Polar Sink permits all factions and is never a battle site.

UN26.text: Play Hajr immediately after your normal force movement during your own turn to make an additional on-planet movement. Reassess ornithopter access when that extra movement begins, so reaching a city with the first move can extend the second.

4GAT.text: After everyone has shipped and moved, opposing forces in the same territory must fight until only one faction or no forces remain. Do not battle in Polar Sink, under the storm, or across the storm. Advanced Bene Gesserit advisors neither fight nor require a battle.

SL4J.text: Starting with First Player, each faction becomes aggressor for all battles in which it is involved. The aggressor chooses which of its territories to resolve first and, with several enemies in one territory, which opponent to fight first. When its battles are finished, continue to the right.

MTEW.text: All of a faction's forces in the territory participate as one side unless separated by the storm. You cannot withdraw just because a battle looks unfavorable. Choosing a zero dial is legal, but you still risk your leader, cards and all forces if you lose.

item-1.text: Dial a number from zero up to the legal strength of your forces in the territory. In Basic play, each force is worth one and the winner loses that many force tokens. Advanced play uses spice support and special-force values.

item-2.text: Include one available leader disc, or a Cheap Hero worth zero instead. If any leader or Cheap Hero can be used, you must include one.

item-3.text: You may include one weapon, one defense, both or neither. A Worthless Card may fill either the weapon or defense place without an effect. You may play two Worthless Cards, one in each place.

item-4.text: When both sides are ready, reveal the plans simultaneously.

KCUS.text: If you have no usable leader or Cheap Hero, announce it. You still dial and battle, but cannot include Treachery Cards in the plan. Cards played outside the plan follow their own timing.

DGPF.text: A living leader can fight several battles in one territory during a phase, but cannot fight in two different territories that phase. Leave surviving leader discs by the territory as reminders, then retrieve them when all battles are finished. A Cheap Hero is discarded after use even by a winner.

G8CB.text: Sources: gf9-base-2019, p. 10; gf9-base-2019, p. 11; gf9-faq-2020-11, p. 8; revised-v2.3, p. 12.

JP89.text: Bene Gesserit Voice is used before Atreides Prescience. Voice gives one instruction about a card or category to play or not play. If the opponent cannot comply, it may make an otherwise legal plan. Voice does not allow extra cards or remove the need for a leader.

922A.text: Atreides may then ask for one chosen element: leader, weapon, defense or number dialed. An answer of no weapon or no defense uses the question; Atreides cannot choose another element. The revealed element must be honored.

T5G3.text: Truthtrance may be played at any time in this interaction. A player may revise the parts of its plan not fixed by Voice, Prescience or Truthtrance. The revealed plans still need to be legal.

UUYT.text: When expansion cards have alternate roles, Prescience sees the role actually used. For example, Weirding Way alongside another weapon is the defense, so an Atreides weapon question reveals the other weapon. Special No-Field rules prevent asking for the number dialed in the relevant battle.

A97L.text: If a later legal effect makes a Prescience answer impossible to honor, give a new legal answer to that same question before reveal. If the original answer remains possible, keep it.

item-1.text: Reveal any traitor calls first. A valid traitor overrides the ordinary result, including weapons and a lasgun-shield explosion.

item-2.text: If no traitor overrides the plans, resolve weapons and defenses. An unprotected leader killed by a weapon contributes no strength. Both leaders may die.

item-3.text: Add each side's dialed strength to its surviving leader's strength and any applicable effect. The higher total wins; a tie goes to the aggressor.

item-4.text: Send every losing force in the territory to the Tanks. The winner loses only the forces committed by its dial, using the correct basic or advanced values. A side can win while losing all its own forces.

item-5.text: Place killed leaders face up in the Tanks. The winner takes spice from the Bank equal to the values of leaders killed in that battle, including its own leader if killed. A surviving losing leader stays alive.

item-6.text: The loser discards every Treachery Card used in its plan. The winner may keep or discard its played battle cards unless a card explicitly says it must be discarded. Then apply any applicable post-battle faction advantage.

MXY7.text: In the Advanced Game, both sides pay the support spice in their plans, win or lose, except a traitor-winning side keeps its committed spice. Taking leader rewards does not refund battle support.

VSRP.text: If your opponent uses a leader matching a traitor card you hold, you may reveal it and call treachery. Revealing is optional. A selected traitor stays a traitor for the entire game, including after revival.

HRS8.text: The side revealing the traitor wins immediately, keeps its forces and committed support spice, sends the traitorous leader to the Tanks and collects that leader's printed strength in spice. It may retain or discard its battle cards under the normal winner rule.

XX54.text: The betrayed side loses all forces in the territory, its committed support spice and all cards in its plan. The winner's leader survives even if the revealed weapons would have killed it. A lasgun-shield combination is overridden.

YM4F.text: If each side reveals the other's leader as a traitor, neither wins: both lose all forces in the territory, both leaders and all played cards. Neither collects leader spice.

GRHC.text: Harkonnen may call a traitor against its ally's opponent. An Atreides leader accompanied by the Kwisatz Haderach cannot turn traitor. Face Dancers are an expansion ability resolved after a battle and are not ordinary traitor calls.

QHTN.text: Keep a revealed Traitor Card. It remains yours and may betray the same leader again after revival. In an allied Harkonnen call, the faction actually fighting is the battle winner and receives the traitorous leader's spice.

M5GM.text: A defense protects only the leader, not the dialed forces. A killed leader adds zero, but the force dial still counts. If both leaders die, compare the dials; the aggressor wins a tie.

NE5L.text: A Lasgun with any Shield in the same battle, including its own side's Shield, explodes. Destroy all spice and forces in the territory, including uninvolved forces and advisors. Kill the leaders used in that battle. Neither side wins or collects spice for killed leaders. A traitor call can override this explosion.

WZWD.text: Keep previously used surviving leaders beside the territory to enforce their movement restriction. They are markers of a previous battle, not leaders participating in a later battle there. A later lasgun-shield explosion does not kill those earlier surviving leaders.

TUDB.text: Expansion weapons and defenses have special definitions. A card that counts as projectile defense is not automatically a Shield. Read its actual categories when resolving Voice, Lasgun or Artillery Strike.

RTGM.title: Support forces with spice | Advanced game

HNW9.text: An ordinary force contributes one-half strength without support, or one strength when supported with one spice. Secretly put the spice committed to support on your battle wheel. You cannot support forces using spice that is not yet spendable.

TWUN.text: The dial is the total strength committed, not the number of tokens. Half points are legal. For example, three ordinary forces supported with one spice can contribute two strength: one supported force and two unsupported forces.

BYNU.text: If you win, select losses whose strength matches the dial and whose support matches the spice committed. You may choose among several valid combinations; you are not required to remove a predetermined token for each spice.

BN7U.title: Support forces with spice, continued | Advanced game

F59N.title: Example
F59N.text: The Emperor has one Sardaukar and five ordinary forces, dials three and commits one spice. After winning it may lose the supported Sardaukar plus two unsupported ordinary forces, or one supported ordinary plus four unsupported ordinary forces. Both remove three strength with one spice supported.

FEJS.text: A Karama played before reveal can make Sardaukar or Fedaykin ordinary for that battle. A separate cancellation can remove the Fremen no-spice advantage. Recalculate the legal maximum and losses using the advantage actually canceled.

7EV5.text: Sources: gf9-base-2019, p. 13; gf9-base-2019, p. 16; gf9-base-2019, p. 19; gf9-faq-2020-11, p. 3; gf9-faq-2020-11, p. 7; gf9-ixian-tleilaxu, p. 9.

YJPN.text: During Spice Collection, a faction with forces in the same territory and sector as spice can take it from the board and put it behind its shield. Its rate is two spice per force, or three per force if it currently occupies Arrakeen or Carthag. City access can help a collecting group elsewhere.

BEZV.text: Take no more than the spice actually present. Leave any excess spice on the board. Collecting forces stay where they are; collection does not return them to reserves or move them out of danger.

SMCN.text: Advanced Bene Gesserit advisors cannot collect spice or provide ornithopters. Faction and module exceptions, such as Ixian Cyborgs or discovery locations, state their own rates or income.

JKMG.title: Advanced stronghold income
JKMG.text: The current occupant of Arrakeen takes two spice, Carthag takes two, and Tuek's Sietch takes one from the Bank each collection phase. Collect for each qualifying stronghold occupied. This income is additional to spice harvested by forces and is absent in the Basic Game.

CPFP.text: Sources: gf9-base-2019, p. 11; gf9-base-2019, p. 13; gf9-base-2019, p. 18; gf9-faq-2020-11, p. 2.

76PJ.text: At the start of the Mentat Pause, move deferred bribe spice from in front of your shield to behind it. Resolve the end-of-turn actions of the factions and modules in use, then check victory using the resulting position.

GQKQ.text: An unallied faction occupying at least three strongholds wins. A two-faction alliance occupying four distinct strongholds wins jointly. Advisors do not count, and a stronghold disputed by factions unable to battle because of storm does not count for either side.

AVL2.text: If several players or alliances meet their requirements together, they share the win. The group may instead agree to play another whole turn, optionally increasing the requirement. Holding more strongholds does not automatically beat another qualifying faction.

LQ22.text: Bene Gesserit's correct faction-and-turn prediction replaces the predicted normal victory with a sole Bene Gesserit win. A normal victory on turn ten takes priority over end-of-game special victories.

G8YZ.text: If nobody has won before the end of turn ten, check the Fremen special condition first. If it is satisfied, Fremen and its ally win. Otherwise Spacing Guild and its ally win if the Guild is playing. If Guild is absent, use GF9's printed fallback awarding the Fremen the game if present, otherwise the factions occupying the most strongholds share the win. This fallback is distinct from satisfying the named Fremen Special Victory Condition.

VDCM.text: If no winner is due and turns remain, advance the counter and start the next Storm Phase. Expansion Homeworlds, Tech Tokens, Hidden Mobile Stronghold, discovery strongholds and Ecaz Occupy can affect the victory count.

32CY.text: Players outside the same alliance may make binding spoken deals about legal future actions, information and spice. State the agreement aloud. It cannot authorize an illegal action or transfer forces, leaders, cards or faction advantages unless a separate effect allows that transfer.

WKUD.text: Put a spice bribe in front of the recipient's shield. It cannot be spent until collected at the start of the Mentat Pause. Allies cannot bribe each other; use their permitted purchase or shipment contributions and their specific alliance advantages.

UMAB.text: A player must honor the possible parts of an agreement. If a promise becomes impossible, that part is void. All parties may agree to cancel their deal.

YUNS.text: This reference places bribery in the Advanced Game, following GF9's November 2020 design-intent correction. Players learning the Basic Game may still share information; paid and binding bribery is an advanced rule.

XJ3N.text: After setup and At Start actions are complete, a Karama can stop one use of a faction advantage, including an alliance advantage, when that advantage is attempted. It does not switch the whole faction off for the phase. In battle, play it before plans are revealed.

item-1.text: Pay for any player's shipment at Guild rates, paying the Bank. This changes the price of that shipment; it does not grant a second shipment.

item-2.text: While holding Karama, bid more spice than you have without revealing it. If outbid, keep it. If you win using it, discard it and pay no spice for the purchased card. An eligible bidder can also play it to take the current card.

item-3.text: In the Advanced Game, activate your faction's special Karama power once in the game.

JYMV.text: A full hand cannot buy or take another card with Karama. Richese special auctions disallow Karama purchases. Discard Karama after use. The updated cards supplied with CHOAM & Richese replace the core copies.

4N3L.text: Karama does not stop a Special Victory Condition or the Bene Gesserit prediction. It cannot reduce Harkonnen's hand limit or stop an ordinary traitor reveal in Harkonnen's own battle. Use the following faction reference for the actions it can cancel.

U5CJ.text: Karama does not cancel the ordinary effect of a Treachery Card such as Hajr, or another faction's Special Karama Power. Stopping Bene Gesserit from converting a Worthless Card is a cancellation of its faction advantage. After an advantage is canceled, its player may choose a revised legal action that respects that cancellation.

JGZS.text: Sources: gf9-faq-2020-11, p. 7; gf9-faq-2020-11, p. 8; gf9-choam-richese, p. 4; revised-v2.3, p. 39.
