cellsByColumnId.column-3: Cannot stop activation after the seventh battle loss

cellsByColumnId.column-2: One Voice, advisor shipment or flip; charity above normal eligibility; using one Worthless Card as Karama
cellsByColumnId.column-3: Cannot cancel prediction; a prevented Worthless Karama is discarded

cellsByColumnId.column-2: Receiving one card payment; giving spice to an ally for the affected use; granting three extra allied revivals; Sardaukar bonus in one battle
cellsByColumnId.column-3: Stopping spice-giving does not remove normal allied purchase or shipment aid

cellsByColumnId.column-2: Two-territory movement; protection/riding against one worm; inspecting the next Storm Card; Fedaykin bonus in one battle
cellsByColumnId.column-3: Cannot cancel ordinary reserve placement or special victory; revealed Storm Card still determines distance

ZBSZ.title: Karama against the base factions, continued

cellsByColumnId.column-2: Bonus card after one purchase; traitor call in an ally's battle; capture after one battle
cellsByColumnId.column-3: Cannot stop an eight-card hand, its own traitor reveal, or use of an already captured leader

cellsByColumnId.column-2: One payment, discount or special shipment; out-of-order shipment and movement
cellsByColumnId.column-3: Cannot stop special victory; canceling out-of-order action makes it use normal storm order for that turn.

YE3Z.text: The precise advantage named matters. Canceling Fedaykin's doubled value does not also cancel all Fremen battle advantages. Benefits with separate triggers require their own cancellation. Expansion factions and homeworld abilities have their own limits.

U6NJ.text: Sources: gf9-faq-2020-11, p. 7; revised-v2.3, p. 17; revised-v2.3, p. 18; revised-v2.3, p. 19.

DEJC.text: Each faction other than Bene Gesserit may spend a Karama on its special power once per game. This is an alternative to the card's normal uses, not an additional effect. Bene Gesserit's conversion of Worthless Cards is a repeatable advantage and gives it no separate once-per-game power.

cellsByColumnId.column-2: Battle, before plan reveal
cellsByColumnId.column-3: Inspect one player's entire battle plan.

cellsByColumnId.column-2: Revival
cellsByColumnId.column-3: Revive up to three forces or one leader for free.

cellsByColumnId.column-2: Spice Blow and Nexus
cellsByColumnId.column-3: Place a worm in a chosen sand territory, destroy spice and unprotected other forces, permit Fremen riding, and generate a phase-end Nexus.

cellsByColumnId.column-2: Bidding
cellsByColumnId.column-3: Take up to four random cards from another player, combine them with your hand, then return the same number of cards of your choice. Returned cards may be ones just taken.

cellsByColumnId.column-2: Shipment and Movement
cellsByColumnId.column-3: Stop one other player's off-planet shipment.

88VJ.text: Harkonnen may temporarily handle the taken cards even with a full hand; returning the same number restores the limit. The power does not let it permanently exceed eight. The Emperor's special revival still observes the one-Sardaukar-per-turn restriction.

HBGP.text: Start with ten forces in Arrakeen, ten in reserves, ten spice and one Treachery Card. Free revival is two forces. Keep the Spice and Treachery decks nearby, since your prescience involves them.

item-1.text: Before bidding begins on each normal auction card, inspect that card. You alone may keep written records about Treachery Cards. You may share information you learn.

item-2.text: At the start of Shipment and Movement, before anyone moves, inspect the single top card of the Spice Deck.

item-3.text: In each of your battles, require the opponent to reveal one element of its plan: leader, weapon, defense or dial. Asking about an absent weapon or defense still uses the question.

item-4.text: For your ally's battle, you may require its opponent to show your ally one element of the plan.

5ZSH.title: Expansion interaction
5ZSH.text: Against a Richese No-Field in battle you may not inspect the number dialed. With two spice blows, your next-card inspection is still only one card. Apply Voice before your battle question.

K5XC.text: Sources: gf9-base-2019, p. 17; gf9-base-2019, p. 23; gf9-faq-2020-11, p. 3; gf9-choam-richese, p. 6.

GKKC.title: Activate the Kwisatz Haderach | Advanced game

GG7H.text: Secretly track Atreides force tokens lost in battles. Once at least seven have been lost, the Kwisatz Haderach becomes active immediately, so it can help in a later battle of the same turn. Storm and worm losses are not battle losses.

APWJ.text: In one territory per turn, accompany an Atreides leader or Cheap Hero with the token to add two strength. It cannot fight alone. If the accompanied leader or Cheap Hero is killed, the token adds nothing to that battle. An accompanied leader cannot turn traitor.

APUX.text: Only a lasgun-shield explosion kills the Kwisatz Haderach. It then requires revival for two spice. This ruleset follows normal leader eligibility for that revival, with Ghola and Tleilaxu exceptions. Its life or death never counts when deciding whether the five Atreides leaders qualify for normal revival.

LHKQ.text: The special Atreides Karama power allows inspection of one player's whole battle plan before reveal. It is separate from the one-element battle question and may be used once per game.

H3BP.text: Sources: gf9-base-2019, p. 17; gf9-base-2019, p. 14; gf9-faq-2020-11, p. 3; gf9-faq-2020-11, p. 6; revised-v2.3, p. 27.

LGQ7.text: In Basic play start with one force in Polar Sink, nineteen in reserve, five spice and one Treachery Card. Free revival is one force.

GAXA.text: After player positions are set, secretly select one other faction and one turn number. If that faction earns a normal victory, alone or in an alliance, on the chosen turn, reveal your prediction and win alone instead. You may predict your eventual ally. You cannot predict a Guild or Fremen special end-game victory, and may win normally if your prediction fails.

FF6R.text: Whenever another faction ships from off-planet to Arrakis, you may send one reserve force for free to Polar Sink. This is additional to your own normal shipment. Fremen reserve placement and Guild cross-shipment do not qualify as off-planet shipment.

TNP7.text: In battle, Voice your opponent to play or not play one weapon, defense, Worthless Card or Cheap Hero as specified. A legal category instruction can name poison weapon, projectile weapon, poison defense or Shield. Special cards can require exact names. If compliance is impossible, the opponent may play an otherwise legal plan.

3TJM.text: You may Voice the opponent in your ally's battle. Give the Voice before Atreides asks its Prescience question. You do not gain the ally's other advantages.

ZFJG.title: Bene Gesserit advisors and fighters | Advanced game

SSPY.text: After Fremen places its forces, put one advisor in any territory, leaving nineteen in reserve. If it is alone it becomes a fighter. All your forces in a territory must show the same side.

6ECV.text: You receive two spice in every CHOAM Charity Phase regardless of holdings. You may use any Worthless Card as a Karama. You have no separate special Karama power.

A74Q.text: An advisor coexists peacefully with other forces. It cannot fight, collect spice, count toward stronghold control or the two-faction limit, provide ornithopters, or enable Family Atomics. It can be lost to storm, worm, a lasgun-shield explosion or atomics.

JXM2.text: When accompanying another faction's off-planet shipment, you may put a free advisor in its destination instead of Polar Sink. That new accompanying advisor cannot flip to a fighter during the same turn unless it becomes alone.

WJ6Z.text: If you already have fighters at the destination of an off-planet shipment, first use Intrusion to flip them to advisors before sending an accompanying advisor there. Otherwise send the free force to Polar Sink or decline it; you may not place the two types together.

item-1.text: Whenever advisors become alone in a territory, flip them to fighters.

item-2.text: After Spice Blow and Nexus but before anyone ships, announce each territory in which you wish to fight and flip all advisors there to fighters. Do not flip under storm or in an ally's territory.

item-3.text: When another faction ships, moves or rides into a territory containing your fighters, you may immediately flip them to advisors, including when that faction was already present and adds more forces.

ZVCS.title: Bene Gesserit advisors and fighters, continued | Advanced game

item-4.text: Advisors moving into an occupied territory may stay advisors or become fighters. Fighters entering a territory without your advisors remain fighters.

item-5.text: Forces moved or shipped into a territory already containing your forces must end as the same type as those already there. Thus fighters joining your advisors flip to advisors.

N7FB.text: The alliance restriction still applies to advisors. Their lack of battle strength does not allow indefinite co-occupation with an ally under this reference's chosen official ruling. Homeworlds cannot receive advisors.

RBSP.text: Sources: gf9-base-2019, p. 18; gf9-faq-2020-11, p. 3; gf9-faq-2020-11, p. 4; gf9-ecaz-moritani, p. 10.

7QMF.text: Start with all twenty forces in reserves, ten spice and one Treachery Card. Free revival is one force.

C58S.text: Other factions pay their normal Treachery auction purchases to you. They must pay the full winning bid; you cannot discount it. Pay the Bank for your own normal purchases.

VX6A.text: You may give spice directly to your ally, for any reason and at any time. It goes behind the ally's shield and is immediately usable. This is separate from normal allied contributions to purchases and shipments.

MVVM.text: During Revival, you may pay for up to three additional forces for your ally. These are extra to its normal three-force ceiling, allowing six in the base game. Pay two spice per ordinary force, redirected to Tleilaxu if its revival payment ability applies.

YFZS.title: Advanced Sardaukar
YFZS.text: In the Advanced Game, five of your twenty forces are Sardaukar. Each has doubled strength for battle and losses, except against Fremen, when each counts as an ordinary force. Supported Sardaukar is worth two and unsupported one. Revive at most one per turn.

D8KG.title: Special Karama
D8KG.text: Once per Advanced Game during Revival, spend Karama to revive up to three forces or one leader for free.

CQVR.text: Start with ten forces divided as you choose between Sietch Tabr, False Wall South and False Wall West, ten in reserves on Dune's far side, three spice and one Treachery Card. Revive three forces free and do not buy extra base-game revivals.

RXLH.text: For your shipment, bring any number of reserves for free into The Great Flat or one territory within two territory borders of it. Do not count The Great Flat itself against the range. This is your faction's reserve-placement action, rather than a paid off-planet shipment.

TF4L.text: Your normal movement range is two territories. Worm riding is a separate move after a Nexus and does not consume your normal movement. Worms do not devour your forces unless an applicable cancellation removes that protection.

VPJN.text: You may protect your ally against worms and grant it three free revivals during Revival. This reference treats those three as its total free allowance within its normal limit, not three additional forces beyond that limit. Your ally shares your special victory.

GT74.text: At the end of the last turn, if no normal victory occurred, your special victory requires Sietch Tabr and Habbanya Sietch to be occupied only by you or nobody, and Tuek's Sietch not to be occupied by Atreides, Harkonnen or Emperor. Allies do not become Fremen for this test. Richese adds itself to the prohibited Tuek's occupants when that expansion applies; Ecaz has a specific co-occupation exception.

NQNK.text: Sources: gf9-base-2019, p. 16; gf9-faq-2020-11, p. 5; gf9-choam-richese, p. 5; gf9-ecaz-moritani, p. 15.

8UK5.text: After the first dialed storm, secretly select the Storm Card for the next turn. Reveal it at the next Storm Phase, move that distance, return and shuffle it, then select the following card.

CLNE.text: If caught by storm, lose half the affected force tokens, rounding losses up. You may place reserves into your legal landing area under storm and lose half. You cannot use ordinary movement or a worm ride to enter or leave storm.

JAQ3.text: Additional consecutive worms after the first can be placed in sand territories of your choice. They devour other unprotected forces and spice there. Your own forces are immune and may benefit from riding.

XCC7.text: Your three Fedaykin each count as two ordinary forces in battle and losses. All your forces fight at full strength without spice. Only one Fedaykin can be revived each turn.

WM9K.text: Once per game, spend Karama during Spice Blow and Nexus to place a worm in a sand territory. Treat it as a normal worm, including a Nexus at phase end and your riding opportunity. This uses your special power; it is separate from placing additional naturally drawn worms.

JHSU.text: Start with ten forces in Carthag, ten in reserves, ten spice and two Treachery Cards. Free revival is two forces.

5Y7S.text: Keep all four traitor cards dealt at setup, including your own leaders. You may reveal any qualifying opponent leader in your own battles. You may also reveal a traitor against your ally's opponent.

NF9J.text: Your hand limit is eight. Whenever you buy a Treachery Card, draw another from the top of the deck for free if that would not exceed eight. Buying with seven cards fills the hand and gives no extra card. You must pass when full.

F9KU.title: Advanced capture
F9KU.text: After a win, you may randomly take one of the loser's available leaders, including the one just used if alive. Exclude leaders dead in the Tanks or used elsewhere that turn. Inspect it, then either kill it face down for two spice from the Bank or keep it to use once. The face-down death counts as a second death.

9L64.text: A captured leader may be a traitor. If it survives the one battle for you, return it to its own faction. If killed, put it in the Tanks for its own faction. Return all captives immediately when all your own leaders are dead. The captor and original owner know the captive's identity and may disclose it.

3NS7.title: Special Karama
3NS7.text: Once per Advanced Game during Bidding, take up to four cards randomly from another hand, look at them as part of your hand, and give back an equal number of your choice. You may return the same cards.

74N4.text: Start with five forces in Tuek's Sietch, fifteen in reserves, five spice and one Treachery Card. Free revival is one force.

AMPQ.text: Receive payments when other factions ship onto Arrakis from off-planet reserves. Pay the Bank for your own shipments.

5ZZ6.title: Choose one shipment type on your turn

item-1.text: Ship reserves to one destination on Arrakis.

item-2.text: Cross-ship a group from one territory to another, applying normal destination costs and restrictions.

item-3.text: Return a group from one territory to reserves at one spice per two forces.

3HNP.text: For the first two types pay half normal cost, rounding the final cost up. The back-to-reserve rate of one per two is already your stated rate and is not halved again. A one-force shipment to a stronghold costs one spice.

P4CJ.text: Your ally may ship reserves to Arrakis or cross-ship forces on Arrakis at Guild rates, but cannot use your return-to-reserve option. The November FAQ permits allied Fremen to treat its off-board reserve territory as the origin of such a cross-shipment.

6S8E.text: If no one has won when the game ends and the Fremen special victory does not apply, you and your ally win. A correct Bene Gesserit prediction cannot target this special victory.

YXJ5.title: Advanced timing
YXJ5.text: Choose when to take your whole shipment-and-movement turn, first, last or between other factions. Announce only when taking it; do not interrupt the middle of another faction's turn. Other factions retain normal order.

AK8Y.title: Special Karama
AK8Y.text: Once per Advanced Game, stop one other faction's off-planet shipment during Shipment and Movement.

MNPV.text: If Karama stops your out-of-order shipment-and-movement advantage, take your turn in normal storm order. Do not simply retry the same timing advantage in a later gap that turn.

4SJQ.text: Sources: gf9-base-2019, p. 19; gf9-base-2019, p. 23; gf9-faq-2020-11, p. 5.

CARM.text: The base deck has thirty-three physical cards. Repeated copies share rules. The card names below provide the effects needed to use the Basic and Advanced core game; expansion cards are described in their books.

cellsByColumnId.column-1: Crysknife, Maula Pistol, Slip Tip, Stunner
cellsByColumnId.column-2: 1 each

cellsByColumnId.column-1: Chaumas, Chaumurky, Ellaca Drug, Gom Jabbar
cellsByColumnId.column-2: 1 each

cellsByColumnId.column-1: Baliset, Jubba Cloak, Kulon, La La La, Trip to Gamont
cellsByColumnId.column-2: 1 each

cellsByColumnId.column-3: Cancel an advantage or use a listed special benefit

RF7D.text: Return retained battle cards to your hand after resolution. Discard cards whose effects require it; remove Family Atomics from the game after use. The new CHOAM & Richese Karama cards replace the old two copies, rather than adding two more.

57E9.text: Sources: gf9-base-2019, p. 5; treachery-online, p. skin.json: TreacheryCardName_STR 0-32; gf9-choam-richese, p. 4.

FVMH.text: A Worthless Card has no base effect. Play one instead of your weapon or defense, or two to fill both places, to get it out of your hand through battle. The loser discards it; a winner may discard or retain it. You cannot freely discard a Worthless Card outside an effect permitting it.

EX86.text: A Cheap Hero fills the leader position with zero strength. It permits weapon and defense play normally, and can be chosen instead of a living leader. If you have no usable leader but do have a Cheap Hero, you must play it. It cannot fill a weapon or defense place merely to discard it.

6PA5.text: Always discard a Cheap Hero after its battle. Advanced Bene Gesserit may instead play Worthless Cards as Karama. CHOAM has separate expansion uses for specific Worthless Cards.

5NSU.text: Sources: gf9-base-2019, p. 10; gf9-base-2019, p. 23; gf9-base-2019, p. 18; gf9-faq-2020-11, p. 8; revised-v2.3, p. 12.

YRWR.text: At any time, play Truthtrance to publicly ask one player one yes-or-no question about the game. The answer must be truthful and public. Pause play for the answer. A question may use and or or.

S3WE.text: A question about a choice during the current turn binds the player to do everything possible to honor the answer. It cannot bind actions in a later turn. If carrying out the answer becomes impossible under the rules, that obligation ends.

VPE6.text: If the question asks something beyond the player's ability to know or decide, it may answer that it does not know. The questioner may then ask another question or save the card for later. Resolve simultaneous attempts in storm order.

6VSS.text: Truthtrance can interact with Voice and Prescience before battle reveal. The player can change elements that those effects have not fixed. Discard the card after resolving its use.

VR6E.text: Sources: gf9-base-2019, p. 23; gf9-faq-2020-11, p. 8; revised-v2.3, p. 39.

GG5D.text: After turn one, play during a Storm Phase before the storm actually moves. You need at least one qualifying force on the Shield Wall or in a territory adjacent to it. Storm between your force's sector and the Shield Wall prevents the connection, but a force or the wall itself being under storm does not by itself prohibit the card.

9ZPR.text: Destroy every force on the Shield Wall and remove the card from the game. Place the Destroyed Shield Wall marker. Arrakeen, Carthag and Imperial Basin lose their protection from storm for the rest of the game. Shield Wall remains rock and can be entered normally.

ULB4.text: You may wait until storm distance is known, then play before movement. The current storm sector is not retroactively hit; vulnerable sectors it moves into are affected. Weather Control and Family Atomics can be played in either order, resolving each in the order played.

A2VJ.text: Advanced Bene Gesserit advisors do not qualify as forces enabling Family Atomics.

5WQW.text: Sources: gf9-base-2019, p. 22; gf9-faq-2020-11, p. 1; gf9-faq-2020-11, p. 8; gf9-base-2019, p. 18; revised-v2.3, p. 39.

cellsByColumnId.column-2: Immediately after your normal force movement during your own Shipment and Movement turn, make one additional on-planet force movement, subject to the normal range, storm and occupancy rules. It may move the same group again or another group.

At any time, revive one of your leaders or up to five of your forces free. This is additional to normal revival and can revive a leader without waiting for all five to be dead. A revived leader may fight immediately. The one-special-force-per-turn limit still applies.
After turn one, before the storm moves, replace its calculated movement with any distance from zero to ten sectors. You may wait until the ordinary distance is known.

H499.text: An extra movement is not an extra shipment. Free revival does not ship the revived forces. Weather Control changes the number of sectors, while storm direction and damage remain normal.

ZAE3.text: Sources: gf9-base-2019, p. 22; gf9-faq-2020-11, p. 1; gf9-faq-2020-11, p. 2; gf9-faq-2020-11, p. 8; revised-v2.3, p. 39; treachery-online, p. skin.json: TreacheryCardDescription_STR 20,22,27.

MS3X.text: The Ixian & Tleilaxu book adds those two factions, Hidden Mobile Stronghold, Cyborgs, Suboids, Face Dancers, Sandtrout, new Treachery Cards and the optional Tech Tokens.

XYRL.text: CHOAM & Richese adds those factions, the Auditor, No-Field tokens, special Richese auctions and card cache, replacement Karama, Poison Tooth and Artillery Strike cards, and the Leader Skill and Advanced Stronghold variants.

GXFF.text: Ecaz & Moritani adds those factions, Ambassadors, Terror, Duke Vidal, Nexus Cards, Homeworlds, discoveries and new Treachery Cards. Its modular variants can be chosen independently.

AJ6E.text: Apply each selected module's setup, timing and exceptions alongside the core sequence. Do not mix KISS, tournament, Landsraad, Dreamrules or other variant changes into GF9 unless choosing that separate ruleset.

A4YR.text: Sources: gf9-ixian-tleilaxu, p. 4; gf9-choam-richese, p. 4; gf9-ecaz-moritani, p. 4; gf9-ecaz-moritani, p. 9.

GB6Q.text: The standard game uses two-faction alliances needing four strongholds. GF9 also lists the following optional arrangements. Choose one before starting; do not change the target midway because an alliance is close to winning.

YTUR.text: With larger alliances, each member still follows the chosen game's payment, movement and public-alliance rules unless the variant explicitly changes them. These alternatives are not the default GF9 alliance requirement.

item-5.text: gf9-ecaz-moritani and ecaz-moritani mean Dune: Ecaz & Moritani Rulebook, Gale Force Nine, supplied copy with 2022 copyright, 16 PDF pages.

78XS.text: Source notes throughout this book use the short labels below. Numeric page references count PDF pages from the front cover as page 1. In the unofficial revised book, the printed rule-page number is two less than the PDF page number. Named references, such as a faction sheet or skin.json entry, identify a section or file location.

item-1.text: gf9-base-2019 means Dune Rulebook, Gale Force Nine, 2019 base edition, 24 PDF pages. The read copy is preserved in the treachery.online document mirror.

item-2.text: gf9-faq-2020-11 and faq-nov2020 mean Dune Questions and Answers, Gale Force Nine, November 2020, 9 PDF pages. Its clarifications inform the rules; its questions and answers are not reproduced here.

item-3.text: gf9-ixian-tleilaxu and ixian-tleilaxu mean Dune: Ixians & Tleilaxu Rulebook, Gale Force Nine, 2020 expansion, 12 PDF pages.

item-4.text: gf9-choam-richese and choam-richese mean Dune: CHOAM & Richese Rulebook, Gale Force Nine, supplied 2021 expansion copy, 12 PDF pages.

item-6.text: revised-v2.3 means Unofficial Revised Dune Rulebook by Van Willis, the supplied file named v2.3. Its internal heading says Version 2.2. It has 44 PDF pages and marks unofficial changes with outlined text. It is a comparison reference, not a new official edition.

item-7.text: compilation means Dune Boardgame Rules Compilation, assembled by Johannes Cassebaum for the Dune Tabletop Discord server, supplied undated copy, 46 PDF pages. It combines the base game, first two expansions and published questions and answers.

item-8.text: treachery-online means the treachery.online community implementation and card reference files by Ronald Ossendrijver and contributors. File locations identify the referenced data, rather than a printed page.

Q424.text: The source copies and community references are linked from the GF9 source ticket: https://github.com/ndelangen/dunezone/issues/2216. The supplied copies identify what was read; a mirror or filename alone does not establish the latest official printing.

LZ4C.text: Conflicting statements and the interpretation adopted for Dune Zone are recorded in GF9 judgements: https://github.com/ndelangen/dunezone/issues/2352. Specific expansion rules apply within their scope. Explicit corrections replace the text they correct. Where the sources disagree, consult that record for the decision, reasons and affected content.

cover.subtitle: Faction rules and the Homeworld, Nexus and Discovery modules for the third GF9 expansion. Read with the GF9 core rulebook.
cover.supportingText: Gale Force Nine rules, with source references and recorded Dune Zone judgements.

W6VC.text: Add Ecaz and Moritani to the available factions. With all three expansions there are 12 choices of faction, but the recommended game remains at most 6 players. Select Homeworlds, Nexus Cards, the new Treachery Cards and Discovery Tokens independently before setup.

cellsByColumnId.column-2: 2 sets, each with a shield, sheet, marker, 5 standard leader discs, 20 troops and 2 Alliance cards.
11 Ambassador tokens.
6 Terror tokens and 1 Atomics Aftermath token.
1 additional strength-6 leader disc, with no Traitor Card.
10 Traitor Cards and 2 Prediction Cards; remove absent factions as usual.
12 Nexus Cards.
13 Homeworld Cards and 13 corresponding reserve discs. Advanced Emperor uses 2; other factions use 1 each.
Reinforcements, Harass & Withdraw and Recruits, 1 each.
7 Spice Cards and 8 Discovery tokens.

HN6V.text: Start with 12 spice, 6 troops in the Imperial Basin and 14 in reserves. Free revival is 2 troops. Take the Ecaz Ambassador and 5 random Ambassadors from the other 10 to form your supply. Keep Ambassador identities public.

TFQL.text: At the end of Revival, place Ambassadors from your supply in strongholds not in storm and without an Ambassador already present. Pay 1 spice for the first token placed that turn, 2 for the second, 3 for the third, and so on. Placement is not troop shipment.

2M2J.text: When another faction enters a stronghold with an Ambassador, you may trigger its effect immediately, interrupting that faction's action. Your ally, Bene Gesserit advisors and the faction matching that Ambassador do not trigger it. Set the triggered token aside after resolving it.

UVWU.text: After all 5 random tokens from your supply have triggered, return them to the unused pool and draw a new random supply of 5. A used Bene Gesserit Ambassador is removed from the game instead. Storms and explosions return affected Ambassadors to your supply. The Ecaz token returns to your supply after use.

BW5X.text: Sources: ecaz-moritani, p. 7; ecaz-moritani, p. 8; ecaz-moritani, p. 15.

cellsByColumnId.column-2: Gain Duke Vidal if he is not in the Tanks, captured or a ghola; or form an alliance with the triggering faction if neither is allied and it agrees. If it allies, you may give it Vidal for this turn. Return this token to your supply.
See the triggering faction's hand.
Use any Ambassador effect that was not in your supply, then remove the Bene Gesserit token from the game.
Discard any number of your Treachery Cards and gain 3 spice per card from the Bank.
Gain 5 spice from the Bank.
Move one group of your troops on Arrakis to any territory, obeying storm and occupancy.
Look at one random Traitor Card held by the triggering faction.
Discard a Treachery Card and draw a replacement from the deck.
If your hand has room, pay the Bank 3 spice and draw the top Treachery Card.
Place up to 4 reserve troops in any territory not in storm for free.
Revive one of your leaders or up to 4 of your troops for free.

FYMB.text: Your alliance advantage lets you choose to have your ally receive the triggered Ambassador's benefit. The Bene Gesserit copied effect can affect a faction that would be immune to the matching token itself.

F3FR.text: Sources: ecaz-moritani, p. 7; ecaz-moritani, p. 8; ecaz-moritani, p. 15.

FX7V.text: While allied, your troops and your ally's troops count as one faction for territory occupancy and may enter and remain together. This allows co-occupation alongside an enemy without breaking the normal two-faction stronghold occupancy limit.

PNAM.text: If you collect desert spice together, divide it by agreement. If you cannot agree, split as evenly as possible and give the odd spice to Ecaz's ally. Co-occupation of Arrakeen or Carthag gives both allies ornithopters and the corresponding collection rate.

W7K4.text: A stronghold occupied by both allies counts only once toward the alliance's total. If both Ecaz and its ally co-occupy each of 3 strongholds, the alliance wins with those 3 rather than needing 4. Ecaz controls a co-occupied stronghold. All 3 Tech Tokens still have to be held by one player to count as a stronghold.

YU3Y.text: Ecaz co-occupying Sietch Tabr with its Fremen ally does not prevent the Fremen special victory. Homeworlds are not territories, so Occupy does not extend to them.

F68G.text: Sources: ecaz-moritani, p. 8; ecaz-moritani, p. 10; ecaz-moritani, p. 15.

3UDE.text: After battle order is established, choose whether Ecaz or its ally is the battling faction. That faction chooses the leader and Treachery Cards and uses its own battle abilities. Battle order and tie priority still depend on the actual battling faction.

DK6V.text: Dial the allied faction's troops normally, then add half the Ecaz troops in the territory, rounded up. The Ecaz contribution needs no spice support. In Advanced play the battling faction pays the applicable support cost for the allied troops; Fremen troops need none. Fedaykin still have their applicable strength.

MDA9.text: If the allied side wins, half the Ecaz troops rounded down remain, and the remainder go to the Tanks. Resolve the ally's troop losses normally. If the allied side loses, its troops are lost under normal losing rules.

73T6.title: Example
73T6.text: With 5 Ecaz troops and 5 Atreides troops, the Atreides dial may receive a bonus of 3 from Ecaz. If the alliance wins, 3 Ecaz troops go to the Tanks and 2 remain. This uses the stated Occupy rule rather than the contradictory worked example in the printed expansion.

7RPL.text: Bene Gesserit advisors remain advisors when applicable; they are not fighting troops for Occupy. Karama played before plans can prevent the battle cooperation: the faction fighting then dials its own troops and the other faction contributes zero. It does not remove the three co-occupied stronghold victory condition.

A3M6.text: Sources: ecaz-moritani, p. 8; ecaz-moritani, p. 15; ecaz-moritani, p. 16.

XNKB.text: Loyalty: before Traitor Cards are dealt, set aside one random Ecaz Traitor Card face up. Never shuffle it into the deck. This is a setup rule and Karama cannot stop it.

PMVC.text: Collection: if you and your ally co-occupy Arrakeen, Carthag or Tuek's Sietch during Spice Collection, each faction receives that stronghold's full collection amount. Karama may stop Ecaz's collection while the ally still collects normally.

8D9M.text: Special Karama: once per game, if you played neither a weapon nor a defense, spend a Karama Card to add the difference between your leader disc's value and your opponent's leader disc's value to your dial. Treat the difference as the absolute gap between the printed values; skill and Kwisatz Haderach additions are separate.

3BE6.text: Sources: ecaz-moritani, p. 4; ecaz-moritani, p. 8; ecaz-moritani, p. 16.

QZ8Z.text: Start with 12 spice. After other factions place their starting troops, put 6 troops in any unoccupied territory and keep 14 in reserves. Free revival is 2 troops. Keep all 6 Terror tokens hidden.

B8J5.text: During Mentat Pause, place one Terror token face down in a stronghold without one, or move one of your existing Terror tokens to a stronghold without one. The stronghold may be in storm. The Hidden Mobile Stronghold and Homeworlds are not legal destinations.

J7KP.text: When another faction other than your ally ships or moves into that stronghold, you may reveal the token and apply its effect to that faction. Advisors and unrevealed No-Field tokens can trigger Terror, even No-Field 0. Adding troops by a Face Dancer reveal or revealing a No-Field already there does not trigger Terror. Terror tokens survive storms and explosions.

X2XD.text: A revealed token is removed from the game after its effect, except when Extortion explicitly returns it. Your own troops cannot trigger your Terror.

MF8J.text: A faction can trigger a token when additional troops enter by shipment or movement even if it already had troops in that stronghold. The trigger is the entering group, not first occupation. Troops placed by another effect, such as the Fremen Homeworld advantage, do not trigger Terror.

VH2W.text: Sources: ecaz-moritani, p. 5; ecaz-moritani, p. 6; ecaz-moritani, p. 14; ecaz-moritani, p. 16.

cellsByColumnId.column-2: Choose a random leader belonging to the entering faction, send it to the Tanks and collect its value in spice. Zoal pays 3.

Send all troops in the territory to the Tanks and place Atomics Aftermath there. No faction may ever ship into that territory again, including Fremen. Reduce Moritani's and its ally's hand limits by 1 from this turn onward; discard a random card if over the new limit.
Take 5 spice from the Bank in front of your shield, usable in Mentat Pause. In Mentat Pause regain this token unless any one player, asked in storm order, pays you 3 spice.
Steal half the entering faction's spice, rounded up, or draw the top Treachery Card, then discard a card of your choice if over your hand limit.
Draw a random card from that faction and discard it if possible. You may then give it a card of your choice from your hand.
Put up to 5 of your reserve troops in the triggering territory for free, obeying storm and occupancy rules. This is allowed even with Atomics Aftermath present.

VKYE.text: Atomics Aftermath bans shipment, including cross-shipment. It does not ban normal on-planet movement or the explicitly allowed Sneak Attack. It is different from the Family Atomics card that destroys the Shield Wall.

M7UK.text: Sources: ecaz-moritani, p. 5; ecaz-moritani, p. 6; ecaz-moritani, p. 14.

8WY4.title: Enemy of My Enemy and alliance

J4BX.text: Before revealing a Terror token triggered by a faction other than Ecaz, you may offer that faction an alliance. If it accepts, break either faction's existing alliance, form the new alliance, and return the unrevealed token to your supply. If it declines, reveal the token and resolve it. This is an exception to forming alliances only during a Nexus.

GNJ2.text: Your ally may keep one Treachery Card played in a battle it loses, provided the battle had a winner and it could have kept that card by winning. A card that must be discarded even by a winner cannot be retained through this benefit.

EKUQ.text: Karama can prevent placing or moving one Terror token, gaining Duke Vidal, or forming an Enemy of My Enemy alliance. It cannot cancel a Terror token's reveal merely because it could prevent placement. If the alliance offer is stopped, you may still reveal the token.

GA7H.text: Assassinate Leaders: after losing a battle in which no traitor was called and the opposing leader disc survived, you may reveal a Traitor Card for another leader of that opponent's faction. If that leader is not already in the Tanks, kill it and collect its value in spice, or 3 for Zoal.

P3SY.text: During Mentat Pause place the revealed card face up as a marker and draw a replacement Traitor Card. Use this advantage at most once against each faction. If you ever reveal a Traitor Card normally, you lose Assassinate Leaders for the rest of the game. It cannot assassinate your own leader captured by Harkonnen, though you may expose that leader as a traitor normally.

P25D.text: Karama cannot prevent Assassinate Leaders. Your special Karama, usable once per game, lets you choose which of the opponent's played Treachery Cards they must keep or discard after you lose a battle.

LAJ8.text: Sources: ecaz-moritani, p. 4; ecaz-moritani, p. 6; ecaz-moritani, p. 14; ecaz-moritani, p. 16.

N2WK.text: Duke Vidal is a strength-6 Ecaz leader with no Traitor Card. Begin with him set aside. Ecaz gains him through its Ambassador; Moritani gains him at the end of Shipment and Movement if Moritani faces battles in at least 2 strongholds, excluding battles against Ecaz, and Vidal is not in the Tanks or otherwise unavailable.

KZ4V.text: Ecaz keeps him until it uses him in a battle or Moritani takes him. Moritani keeps him for one battle, and sets him aside by the end of the turn if he is neither in the Tanks nor captured. Gaining Vidal does not grant a second use after he has fought that turn.

UY4H.text: Only Ecaz may revive Vidal, including with a Ghola Treachery Card. Ecaz may pay 5 spice to revive him regardless of its other leaders. Revival returns him to the set-aside supply; it does not by itself give control. Ecaz may revive its other leaders normally when at least 5 of its leaders, counting Vidal, are in the Tanks, even if one remains alive.

TGT9.text: Sources: ecaz-moritani, p. 3; ecaz-moritani, p. 6; ecaz-moritani, p. 8; ecaz-moritani, p. 9.

V2EK.text: Give each faction its Homeworld Card and reserve disc. Keep reserve troops on that disc. Homeworld cards show a reserve threshold, battle strength for each reserve state, and the effects of High, Low and Occupied. Apply the state that matches the current reserve count as it changes.

F4XJ.text: At or above its printed threshold, use the High effect. Below the threshold, use Low. Low normally increases free revival by 1 and adds 1 spice when the faction actually collects Charity; the extra Charity comes directly from the Bank, not CHOAM. Low does not raise Charity eligibility: a faction with 2 spice still does not qualify merely because the bonus exists.

F569.text: Tupile reverses the usual benefit: CHOAM has a High penalty and a Low advantage. Salusa Secundus gives neither bonus revival nor bonus Charity. Use the exact effects on the Homeworld Cards; they are part of this module's rules.

ZEF9.text: Karama does not cancel Homeworld advantages or penalties. Homeworlds are not Arrakis territories, and Ecaz Occupy, Moritani Terror and other territory-only effects do not extend to them.

YF7L.text: Sources: ecaz-moritani, p. 9; ecaz-moritani, p. 10; ecaz-moritani, p. 15; ecaz-moritani, p. 16.

4EDN.title: Homeworld shipment and occupation | Optional module

U6MV.text: A faction may use its shipment to send reserve troops to another faction's homeworld for 1 spice per troop, or Guild half price. This is the normal shipment for the turn, not an extra shipment. Homeworld shipment triggers Heighliners.

8XDH.text: Only the Spacing Guild may ship troops from Arrakis to a homeworld, as a cross-shipment, unless its Homeworld advantage explicitly grants that service to another faction. Other factions cannot add troops to their own homeworld except through revival. Troops may ship between homeworlds under the module's restrictions.

L4R8.text: An invading faction becomes Occupier after defeating the native faction and retaining troops there, or immediately when alone there. It keeps that status until none of its troops remain. Apply the card's Occupied effect and any Spice Collection income, even in the Basic game. That income comes from the Bank and may immediately be shared with its ally. The native Low penalty remains in effect while occupied.

HYXX.text: No faction may ally with a faction whose troops occupy its homeworld. Allies may neither ship to nor occupy one another's homeworlds. Bene Gesserit cannot send advisors to a homeworld or flip fighters to advisors on another faction's homeworld.

YVBS.text: Sources: ecaz-moritani, p. 9; ecaz-moritani, p. 10; ecaz-moritani, p. 15; ecaz-moritani, p. 16.

5T29.title: Homeworld battles and Emperor reserves | Optional module

VXGX.text: On a homeworld, add its printed battle strength for the native faction's current reserve state to the native dial total. Invaders cannot reveal traitors or Face Dancers there. Native factions retain their applicable traitor rights.

42F9.text: In a Lasgun-Shield explosion, both factions lose and leaders die normally. The invader loses its troops normally. The native faction loses only as many troops as its current printed Homeworld Battle strength, regardless of its dial, and any native troops left remain. For example, High Caladan loses only 2 Atreides troops, matching the Homeworld Card.

7D3E.text: In Basic play the Emperor uses only Kaitain and treats Sardaukar as ordinary troops. In Advanced play add Salusa Secundus. Start Sardaukar there, and revive Sardaukar there; normal troops start and revive on Kaitain. A shipment may draw from both worlds. The Emperor may use its normal movement to move troops between the two worlds.

8M6Y.text: Salusa Secundus uses the printed overlapping reserve bands: from High flip Low below 2 Sardaukar; from Low flip High above 2. At exactly 2 keep its current state. This exception needs the card's two thresholds to be understood together.

PML8.text: If Kaitain is Low and occupied, apply both divisions of its income. For a 5-spice Treachery payment, the Emperor receives 3 and the Occupier 2. Harkonnen's Homeworld collection benefit pays a total of 2 spice for the phase when a listed trigger occurs, rather than 2 for every individual trigger.

S2FK.text: After the Spice Blow and Nexus phase, if a Nexus occurred and at least one alliance exists, every unallied player may draw a Nexus Card. A player already holding one may discard it and draw a replacement. Keep it secret until played. Discard it to enter any alliance.

24M2.text: Each card offers one effect according to its named faction. Betrayal applies when another player controls that faction; it cancels the specified advantage when attempted. Cunning applies to your own faction. Secret Ally applies when the named faction is absent. A Secret Ally is the card's effect, not a normal on-board alliance.

NDA7.text: Discard after use. At the end of a later qualifying Nexus you may draw again if still unallied. Shuffle discards when the deck runs out. Whenever you draw your own faction's card, you may immediately discard it and redraw in either Basic or Advanced play; some Cunning effects require Advanced rules.

CEE8.text: Use Bene Gesserit Secret Ally before Atreides Prescience. A Traitor Card gained by Tleilaxu through Harkonnen Secret Ally is a Face Dancer. Moritani Betrayal removes one Terror token anywhere on the board; it does not permanently prevent future Terror placement.

WH3J.title: Optional new Treachery Cards | Optional module

235G.text: Add Reinforcements, Harass & Withdraw and Recruits to the Treachery Deck, one copy each. Discard each after use.

cellsByColumnId.column-2: Play during Revival. All factions double their Free Revival rates. The revival limits is increased to 7. Discard after use.

Play as part of your battle plan in place of a weapon or defense if you have at least 3 forces in reserves. Add 2 to your dialed number, then send 3 forces from reserves to the Tanks. Discard after use.

Play as part of your battle plan in place of a weapon or defense when not on your own Home World. Your undialed forces return to your reserves. Your leader may be killed as normal. If your opponent calls traitor, this effect is cancelled. Discard after use.

XA9G.text: Reinforcements and Harass & Withdraw are placed in a Battle Plan in place of a weapon or a defense, but are neither. If Atreides asks to see that element, answer that no weapon or defense of that type is being played. Resolve the card's printed troop effect. In a co-occupied Ecaz battle, Harass & Withdraw returns only the player's own undialed troops; treat the other ally's troops normally.

5AJH.text: Recruits is played during Revival. Double each faction's current free revival, including its Low Homeworld increase, and use a revival limit of 7 for the turn. A Low Fremen free rate of 4 becomes 8 before the limit, so it may revive 7 free. Recruits does not turn CHOAM's base rate of zero into a free troop unless another effect already increased that rate.

UQ8U.text: Shuffle the 7 Discovery module Spice Cards into the Spice Deck and mix the 8 Discovery tokens face down, keeping Hiereg and Smuggler types available separately. The 7 cards comprise Great Maker and 6 Discovery blows.

TLVS.text: Great Maker resolves like Shai-Hulud against the preceding spice territory, with ordinary protection and first-turn worm rules. Then every player votes in storm order on whether to hold a Nexus. A strict majority of yes votes is required; a tie means no Nexus. Fremen may then ride with any number of reserve troops to any legal territory, instead of riding from the board or placing the worm token. Karama killing Fremen in the devoured territory does not stop the reserve ride.

NJTU.text: A Discovery blow destroys the existing spice and troops in its indicated spice territory, then places 6 spice there subject to the normal storm restriction. Place one random token of the indicated Hiereg or Smuggler type face down at the separate token location and sector shown on the card. Do not assume its token marker is placed at the spice blow itself.

SR3V.title: Revealing and entering Discoveries | Optional module

A3PW.text: During Spice Collection, a faction with non-advisor troops in a token's territory may inspect it and choose whether to reveal it. If left hidden, the opportunity returns in the next Spice Collection. Fremen may inspect hidden Hiereg tokens at any time; Guild may inspect hidden Smuggler tokens at any time.

VZFC.text: Five tokens are locations. Once revealed, leave them in place. Revealing a location does not occupy it. At the beginning of the next turn, before the storm and before Ixian stronghold movement, factions in its parent territory may move any of their non-advisor troops there into the newly revealed location.

AVES.text: Thereafter a location is a territory within its parent. Normal movement must enter the parent and then spend another movement to enter the location. Shipping into a revealed location costs the stronghold rate. Troops inside are immune to storm and sandworms. Jacurutu alone explicitly counts as a stronghold for victory.

cellsByColumnId.column-2: A normal stronghold. After winning a battle here, gain 1 spice per opposing undialed troop sent to the Tanks.
While occupying it during Spice Collection, take 2 spice from the Bank.
While occupying it during Storm, add or subtract 1 from storm movement. It does not change Weather Control.
While occupying it, use Truthtrance as Karama and Karama as Truthtrance.
While occupying it during Spice Collection, steal 1 spice from each spice blow collected.
Draw one Treachery Card. If your hand was full, draw and then discard any card. Remove the token.
Take 7 spice from the Bank and remove the token.
Take the token. In a subsequent turn, spend it to use movement 3 instead of normal movement for one movement action, then remove it.
Ecaz Loyalty in Advanced play; assign optional Leader Skills after starting Treachery.
Place the Ixian stronghold and finish optional Tech Token assignment.
Enter newly revealed Discovery locations, then optional Ixian stronghold movement.
Ecaz may buy and place Ambassadors.
Ambassadors and Terror interrupt entering factions; check Moritani's Vidal condition at the end.

cellsByColumnId.column-1: End of Spice Blow and Nexus
cellsByColumnId.column-2: Qualifying unallied players draw or replace Nexus Cards after alliances are formed.
Inspect and optionally reveal Discoveries; apply Homeworld and location collection.
Resolve faction pause effects and check victory with current strongholds, Homeworld victory effects and optional Tech Tokens.

ZSUC.text: Use each optional card's exact text with the procedures above. A module does not automatically activate another module. In particular, Discovery locations are not Homeworlds, Terror is not Family Atomics, and a Secret Ally card is not an ordinary faction alliance.

VH88.text: Sources: ecaz-moritani, p. 4; ecaz-moritani, p. 9; ecaz-moritani, p. 11; ecaz-moritani, p. 12; ecaz-moritani, p. 13; ecaz-moritani, p. 14.

CCQA.text: Source notes throughout this book use the short labels below. Numeric page references count PDF pages from the front cover as page 1. In the unofficial revised book, the printed rule-page number is two less than the PDF page number. Named references, such as a faction sheet or skin.json entry, identify a section or file location.

item-2.text: gf9-faq-2020-11 and faq-nov2020 mean Dune Questions and Answers, Gale Force Nine, November 2020, 9 PDF pages. Its clarifications inform the rules; its questions and answers are not reproduced here.

item-3.text: gf9-ixian-tleilaxu and ixian-tleilaxu mean Dune: Ixians & Tleilaxu Rulebook, Gale Force Nine, 2020 expansion, 12 PDF pages.

item-4.text: gf9-choam-richese and choam-richese mean Dune: CHOAM & Richese Rulebook, Gale Force Nine, supplied 2021 expansion copy, 12 PDF pages.

item-5.text: gf9-ecaz-moritani and ecaz-moritani mean Dune: Ecaz & Moritani Rulebook, Gale Force Nine, supplied copy with 2022 copyright, 16 PDF pages.

item-6.text: revised-v2.3 means Unofficial Revised Dune Rulebook by Van Willis, the supplied file named v2.3. Its internal heading says Version 2.2. It has 44 PDF pages and marks unofficial changes with outlined text. It is a comparison reference, not a new official edition.

item-7.text: compilation means Dune Boardgame Rules Compilation, assembled by Johannes Cassebaum for the Dune Tabletop Discord server, supplied undated copy, 46 PDF pages. It combines the base game, first two expansions and published questions and answers.

item-8.text: treachery-online means the treachery.online community implementation and card reference files by Ronald Ossendrijver and contributors. File locations identify the referenced data, rather than a printed page.

CRR8.text: The source copies and community references are linked from the GF9 source ticket: https://github.com/ndelangen/dunezone/issues/2216. The supplied copies identify what was read; a mirror or filename alone does not establish the latest official printing.

DSPE.text: Conflicting statements and the interpretation adopted for Dune Zone are recorded in GF9 judgements: https://github.com/ndelangen/dunezone/issues/2352. Specific expansion rules apply within their scope. Explicit corrections replace the text they correct. Where the sources disagree, consult that record for the decision, reasons and affected content.

cover.subtitle: Faction rules, cards and optional Tech Tokens for the first GF9 expansion. Read with the GF9 core rulebook.
cover.supportingText: Gale Force Nine rules, with source references and recorded Dune Zone judgements.

P5GU.text: Add Ixians and Tleilaxu to the available factions. Choose which factions will play before building the Traitor and Prediction decks. This expansion adds choices of faction, not a requirement to play with more players. Use its faction rules in either the Basic or Advanced game; abilities marked Advanced apply only in the Advanced game.

6YFJ.text: Tech Tokens are a separate optional module. Decide whether to use them before setup. Retain the core turn sequence and all core rules except where an expansion rule gives an exception.

cellsByColumnId.column-2: 2 sets, each with a shield, sheet, player marker, 5 leader discs and 20 troops.
7 Cyborgs and 13 Suboids, plus the Hidden Mobile Stronghold.
14 additions. If using the CHOAM & Richese replacement Poison Tooth and Artillery Strike, replace the earlier copies.
1 Sandtrout, shuffled into the Spice Deck.
11 additions: 5 per new faction and a Cheap Hero traitor. Exclude absent factions as usual.
2 faction additions.
3 optional tokens: Axlotl Tanks, Heighliners and Spice Production.

C4DA.text: Start with 10 spice. Of your 7 Cyborgs and 13 Suboids, place 3 of each in the Hidden Mobile Stronghold. Your other 4 Cyborgs and 10 Suboids start in reserves. After the first storm movement, place the stronghold pointing at a sector of any non-stronghold territory, including the Polar Sink.

F65U.text: Before starting Treachery Cards are dealt, draw one card per faction in the game. Keep one, shuffle the remainder and deal one to every other faction. Harkonnen then receive their additional starting card from the deck. This replaces the normal one-card starting deal.

2H6E.text: Your free revival is 1 troop, either a Cyborg or a Suboid. Both types pay normal shipment costs. A paid Cyborg revival costs 3 spice; paid Suboid revival uses the normal troop cost.

PRKC.text: Sources: ixian-tleilaxu, p. 8; ixian-tleilaxu, p. 9; ixian-tleilaxu, p. 11.

3VC6.text: Before the Bidding round, draw one more Treachery Card than the number of normal cards to be auctioned and inspect them. Return one card of your choice face down to either the top or bottom of the deck. Shuffle the remaining drawn cards to form the auction supply. You know which cards are in the auction, but their shuffled order is secret.

WCTU.text: After an ally buys a card in normal bidding, they may inspect it, immediately discard it and draw the top card of the Treachery Deck. Make the decision separately for each purchase. This applies to a Richese Black Market purchase, even if that card is Richese technology, but not to a purchase from the separate Richese cache.

8Q9F.title: With Richese
8Q9F.text: Richese announces whether their cache card comes first or last before the Ixian Bidding advantage. Draw one fewer normal auction card for each cache or successfully sold Black Market card replacing a normal card. The Ixian extra draw still supplies one card to return to the deck.

cellsByColumnId.column-2: 7 troops. Each is worth 2 normal troops in Basic battle, moves up to 2 territories, and collects up to 3 spice.
13 troops. Each is worth 1/2 in battle. Move up to 2 territories with at least one Cyborg, otherwise 1, subject to normal ornithopter movement. Collect spice normally.

VKQC.text: Pay battle losses in the battle strength of the troops removed. After calculating losses, exchange any surviving Suboids in the battle territory one for one for Cyborgs lost in that battle. Send the exchanged Suboids to the Tanks and retain those Cyborgs.

4QUT.title: Example
4QUT.text: With 2 Cyborgs and 6 Suboids, a dial of 6 can cost both Cyborgs and 4 Suboids. Exchange the 2 surviving Suboids for the 2 lost Cyborgs. The surviving force is 2 Cyborgs.

PJ6H.text: Suboids still occupy territories, control strongholds and collect spice despite their fractional battle strength.

LUHZ.text: The Hidden Mobile Stronghold is a separate stronghold inside the non-stronghold territory it points at. Its position and occupants are public. Occupying it counts as one stronghold toward victory, and troops inside are protected from sandworms and the storm.

RU9A.text: On later turns, before storm movement is dialed or revealed, if Ixian troops occupy the stronghold, the Ixians may move it up to 3 territories, ending with its pointer in a sector of a non-stronghold territory. It may not move into, out of or through the storm. Troops outside do not board it merely because it passes them.

GVHL.text: When it moves into, out of or through a spice-bearing sector, immediately collect up to 2 spice per troop inside, taking spice from that territory. The pointer must pass through the sector that actually holds the spice. This is the stronghold movement collection rule; Cyborg collection capacity of 3 applies to ordinary Spice Collection.

SVUF.text: Ixians may ship directly into it at the stronghold shipment rate. Other factions must first ship or move to its parent territory and then spend one territory of movement to enter. Capturing the stronghold does not let another faction move it. Bene Gesserit Spiritual Advisors may accompany an Ixian shipment directly inside. Fremen worm riding may also end directly inside, subject to storm and occupancy rules.

BTN4.text: Pointing at the Polar Sink does not make the stronghold part of the neutral Polar Sink. Battles can occur inside the stronghold. Moritani cannot place a Terror token inside it.

MCAF.text: Cyborgs need spice support to count at their full strength of 2. Without support they count as 1. Suboids always count as 1/2 and cannot be increased by paying spice. Their support cost is zero.

NSWR.text: Technology: once per Bidding round, before bidding begins on a normal card and before Atreides inspects it, exchange that card for one from your hand. This is a swap, so a full hand does not prevent it. It does not replace the separate Bidding advantage.

A2BA.text: Special Karama: once per game, spend a Karama Card to move the Hidden Mobile Stronghold up to 2 territories during your own Shipment and Movement turn, in addition to your normal movement. Normal stronghold movement restrictions still apply.

item-1.text: Resolve traitors and determine the battle winner first. Whenever another faction wins a battle, you may reveal a Face Dancer matching its leader, including in a battle you did not fight.

BB8U.text: Start with 5 spice and all 20 troops in reserves. Your free revival is 2 troops. You receive no Traitor Cards during ordinary Traitor selection. After other factions have selected traitors and returned unused cards, shuffle the remaining deck and draw 3 Face Dancers.

item-2.text: The battle remains that faction's win. Resolve its card retention, spice for killed leaders and Tech Token claim normally.

item-3.text: Send the revealed leader to the Tanks if not already killed. Collect no spice for killing it through the Face Dancer reveal.

item-4.text: Return that winner's surviving troops in the battle territory to its reserves. Replace up to that number with Tleilaxu troops from your reserves and/or anywhere on Arrakis.

EQXV.text: An Atreides leader accompanied by the Kwisatz Haderach can still be a Face Dancer. Face Dancer replacement is not shipment or movement and does not trigger Terror tokens.

YL7U.text: Keep revealed Face Dancers face up. Do not replace or reuse them individually. After all 3 have been revealed, return all 3 to the Traitor Deck, shuffle and draw 3 new ones. During each Mentat Pause you may instead return one unrevealed Face Dancer to the deck, shuffle and draw a replacement.

MAP8.text: Sources: ixian-tleilaxu, p. 6; ixian-tleilaxu, p. 7; ixian-tleilaxu, p. 10; ixian-tleilaxu, p. 11.

YDCL.text: You have no troop revival limit. Pay the Spice Bank half the normal total revival price, rounded up. Other factions pay their revival costs to you. You may raise another faction's normal 3-troop revival limit to 5; this also lets Fremen buy additional troops up to that limit. Special limits on reviving elite troops still apply.

QGFL.text: For every faction that takes free revival or uses a Ghola Card, take 1 spice from the Spice Bank, including when you take free revival yourself. If the Emperor pays for an ally's extra revivals, those payments also go to you.

EWLR.text: When a faction cannot otherwise revive a leader, it may ask you to revive one specific dead leader, face up or face down. Set a price; if the faction agrees and pays, revive that leader. This allows early revival, not an extra leader revival: at most one leader per faction per Revival phase. When its leaders are all unavailable and normal leader revival is allowed, apply the normal rule instead.

K8BD.text: You may offer your ally half-price troop and leader revival, rounding up the total price. The ally pays you; this alliance benefit does not let you pay the ally's revival bill. CHOAM allied with Tleilaxu may halve its total troop revival price rather than rounding each troop separately.

M4G2.text: Zoal copies the opposing leader disc's value for battle and for spice collected if Zoal is killed. Against a Cheap Hero, Zoal is 0. Do not copy additions from the Kwisatz Haderach or a Leader Skill. Reviving Zoal costs 3 spice. This is the explicit Zoal revival price. Do not halve it again.

XMZU.text: Gholas: while you have fewer than 5 active leaders, you may revive dead leaders belonging to other factions at your discounted price and add them to your pool, up to 5 active leaders in total. Face-down leaders are eligible. You may revive more than one ghola in a Revival phase if there is room in your pool.

M8UE.text: A ghola can be exposed as a traitor by whoever holds its Traitor Card; it does not automatically betray its original faction. A ghola does not earn you a Leader Skill draw. The Auditor and Duke Vidal are excluded from Tleilaxu ghola acquisition.

D2UH.text: A ghola cannot be sold back while alive. After it dies and returns to the Tanks, its owning faction may request revival under the normal Tleilaxu revival arrangement.

2YRX.text: Special Karama: once per game, spend a Karama Card to prevent one player from performing a revival of troops and/or a leader.

M2XG.text: Sources: ixian-tleilaxu, p. 6; ixian-tleilaxu, p. 7; ixian-tleilaxu, p. 10.

E3WU.text: Keep Tech Tokens visible in front of shields. Initially give Axlotl Tanks to Tleilaxu, Heighliners to Ixians, and Spice Production to Fremen. After the first storm movement, assign any token whose faction is absent at random to the next factions in turn order that have no token. No starting faction receives a second token this way.

XAMZ.text: When you defeat a faction holding Tech Tokens, take one. If it holds several, choose which one to take. This transfer follows the battle winner even if a later Face Dancer reveal replaces its troops.

WBPQ.text: One player controlling all 3 tokens counts them as one stronghold for victory. Allied players may not combine their tokens to create this stronghold, including an Ecaz alliance.

cellsByColumnId.column-2: At least one faction takes free revival, except when only Tleilaxu does so.
At least one faction ships from off-planet, except when only the Spacing Guild does so.
At least one faction takes CHOAM Charity, except when only Bene Gesserit and/or CHOAM use their faction Charity advantages.

LNTG.text: Each qualifying token triggers only once in its phase, however many factions qualify. Its income is 1 spice from the Spice Bank for every Tech Token its holder controls. Place that income on the triggering token and collect it at the end of the phase. Inflation does not alter this amount.

Z36U.title: Example
Z36U.text: If you hold Axlotl Tanks and Heighliners and another faction takes free revival, Axlotl Tanks produces 2 spice. If a qualifying shipment later occurs, Heighliners produces 2 more. Multiple qualifying revivals do not multiply the first payment.

X7DA.text: Shuffle Sandtrout into the Spice Deck. When it is drawn, existing alliances end. The next Shai-Hulud produces no Nexus. Look at that worm's replacement: a second Shai-Hulud produces a normal Nexus; a Spice Blow is doubled. A Spice Blow immediately after Sandtrout is not doubled merely because it follows Sandtrout.

YP5F.text: The Cheap Hero Traitor Card can betray any opposing Cheap Hero. After its first reveal, it remains usable against later Cheap Heroes, though everyone knows you hold it.

8ZDM.text: Poison Blade is both a projectile and poison weapon. A Shield alone does not protect against it; Shield Snooper provides the combined protection. Shield Snooper also counts as a Shield for a Lasgun explosion and protects against Artillery Strike. Weirding Way played as a projectile defense is not a Shield: it neither causes a Lasgun explosion nor protects from Artillery Strike.

65U7.text: Poison Tooth is not stopped by a Snooper, but Chemistry played as a poison defense stops it. After seeing battle results, its player may choose not to use it. A winner may keep an unused Poison Tooth; otherwise discard it. Artillery Strike is always discarded after use. Use the corrected CHOAM & Richese versions of those cards when available.

FRBS.text: Bene Gesserit Voice names a special weapon specifically when required, such as Artillery Strike. Chemistry and Weirding Way only count as the type in which they are actually played for Prescience and Leader Skills.

2Q9L.text: Voice may name a generic projectile or poison weapon, Shield or Snooper, or the exact special card. Poison Blade, Poison Tooth, Shield Snooper, Weirding Way and Chemistry can be prohibited through the generic type stated on the card. Artillery Strike and Lasgun must be named specifically; a command simply banning all special cards is invalid. Voice can compel Weirding Way in its default projectile-weapon role, but cannot force its conversion into a defense. Chemistry defaults to poison defense and cannot be forced into its alternate weapon role. Voice may prohibit either alternate role when it applies.

cellsByColumnId.column-2: Weapon - Special - Play as part of your Battle Plan. This weapon counts as both projectile and poison. You may keep this card if you win this battle.
Weapon - Projectile - Play as part of your Battle Plan. Kills opponent's leader before battle is resolved. Opponent may protect leader with a Shield. You may keep this card if you win the battle.
Weapon - Poison - Play as part of your Battle Plan. Kills opponent's leader before battle is resolved. Opponent may protect leader with a Snooper. You may keep this card if you win the battle.

Weapon - Special - Play as part of your Battle Plan. Counts as a projectile weapon but has the same effect as a projectile defense when played as a defense with another weapon. You may keep this card if you win this battle.

Weapon - Special - Play as part of your Battle Plan. Kills both leaders, and is not stopped by a Snooper. After seeing the battle results, you may choose not to use this weapon in which case you don't need to discard it if you win the battle.
Defense - Special - Play as part of your Battle Plan. Counts as both a Shield (projectile defense) and Snooper (poison defense). You may keep this card if you win this battle.

Defense - Special - Play as part of your Battle Plan. Counts as a poison defense but has the same effect as a poison weapon when played as a weapon with another defense. You may keep this card if you win this battle.

Weapon - Special - Play as part of your Battle Plan. Kills both leaders (no spice is paid for them). Both players may use Shields to protect their leader against the Artillery Strike. Surviving (shielded) leaders do not count towards the battle total, the side that dialed higher wins the battle. Discard after use.
Play just after a spice blow comes up. Doubles the Spice blow. Place double the amount of spice in the territory.
Play at beginning of Spice Blow Phase instead of revealing the Spice Blow card. Causes a Shai-Hulud to appear. Play proceeds as though Shai-Hulud has been revealed.
At the beginning of any phase, cause all players to discard half of the spice behind their shields, rounded up, to the Spice Bank.
Worthless Card - Play as part of your Battle Plan, in place of a weapon, defense, or both. This card has no value in play, and you can discard it only by playing it in your Battle plan.

PZAA.text: The 14-card expansion has 12 named designs; deck membership supplies repeated copies. Poison Tooth and Artillery Strike use the corrected versions explained above. Harvester doubles a qualifying blow; it does not increase spice protected by a different rule. Thumper is played before the ordinary Spice Card draw and resolves as a Shai-Hulud draw, with first-turn worm restrictions. Amal is played at the beginning of a phase and removes half of each player's behind-shield spice, rounded up.

M97W.text: Karama stops one use of an advantage when attempted, after setup. It does not permanently remove that advantage. Suboids remain half strength, and a special Karama power cannot itself be canceled by another Karama.

6EML.text: Canceling Cyborg strength makes Cyborgs ordinary troops for that battle: strength 1 in Basic, or 1/2 without support and 1 with support in Advanced. The Cyborg strength advantage is inherited from the Basic faction rules; its cancellation still applies in Advanced. Suboids remain 1/2.
